title: Bond Markets Surge as Investors Reassess US AI Tech Sector Growth
summary: Investors have turned to bonds as analysts have warned about stagnation in the AI and tech sector in U.S. markets, with companies like Intel, Alphabet, Meta, and Amazon all dropping significantly last week, even when the wider economy reported hotter-than-expected Q3 growth numbers. Bonds Surge As A...
content:
1. News
  2. Finance
  3. Bond Markets Surge as Investors Reassess US AI Tech Sector Growth

Published:Nov 1, 2026, 9:30 PM EST

Investors have turned to bonds as analysts have warned about stagnation in the AI and tech sector in U.S. markets, with companies like Intel, Alphabet, Meta, and Amazon all dropping significantly last week, even when the wider economy reported hotter-than-expected Q3 growth numbers.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 1, 2026, 9:30 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Investors are rushing to bonds as tech and artificial intelligence (AI) stocks slump, driving 10-year real yields to a low of 2.58%.
  • Economists warn that global market growth is dangerously dependent on inflated AI and tech expenditures.
  • Experts predict an AI bubble burst will trigger a market drawdown and force a massive US government bailout.

Bonds Surge As A Hedge Against US AI Sector Stagnation

While the US economy reported hotter-than-expected growth numbers during the last quarter, surprising some, investors are concerned about the source of this growth and how it might stagnate in the coming months.

According to the Financial Times, the bond trade has been growing after the recent recoil in the tech AI sector driven by companies like Intel, Meta, Amazon, and Alphabet, which all experienced relevant drops in market capitalization last week. This took real yields to reach seasonal lows, with the 10-year numbers reaching as low as 2.58% this week.

This effect is explained by more investors rushing to bonds as they reassess the capabilities of the U.S. tech/AI sector to keep growing, betting on these performing better than stocks.

“The market had been underwriting strong growth — underpinned by AI and the expectation that there would be some relief in the Middle East — and now we’re re-evaluating some of the growth expectations,” said Bill Campbell, portfolio manager at DoubleLine.

Jason Granet, chief investment officer and head of credit services at BNY, also referred to investor worries about these AI companies having the ability to maintain their growth levels moving forward. “Because AI companies grew so much last year, it will be harder to beat those numbers. Growth may be decelerating, but it doesn’t necessarily signal weakness in the economy,” he declared.

Similarly, other economists showed concerns about the composition of the growth of stock markets in U.S. and global markets, with tech and AI spending increasingly becoming a driving factor.

Vincent Reinhart, chief economist at BNY Investments, assessed that the current state of affairs was worrisome.

“It is so heavily dependent on technology expenditure. And it is not just a U.S. phenomenon; it’s a global phenomenon. You don’t have to be a tech pessimist to be worried,” he declared.

Not only traditional economists have warned about the effects of inflated spending on AI and tech in the U.S.

Arthur Hayes, co-founder of the now-defunct BitMEX exchange, has also expressed that the inevitable burst of the AI bubble will cause a market drawdown, with the U.S. government ultimately swooping in to save the too-big-to-fail AI giants by printing millions.

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: Mercado Bitcoin Plans Sui Asset Access in Brazil With Lending and Tokenization Links
summary: Mercado Bitcoin and Sui have outlined access to SUI and stablecoins, with USDsui collateral and tokenized assets in scope. A potential Hashi integration remains exploratory.
content:
TL;DR: Mercado Bitcoin and Sui have outlined access to SUI and stablecoins, with USDsui collateral and tokenized assets in scope. A potential Hashi integration remains exploratory.

Sui’s planned expansion through Mercado Bitcoin brings together several different distribution opportunities: access to tokens, conversion between local money and stablecoins, and the possibility of connecting those assets to lending and investment products.

The October 29 announcement is therefore more than a listing headline. It is also a roadmap with elements at different stages, which need to be kept separate when assessing what customers can actually use.

The initial asset connection is clearly defined

The Sui Foundation announcement says Mercado Bitcoin will integrate SUI, USDC and USDsui, supporting purchases, sales and transfers on Sui. It also says USDsui will be eligible collateral in the exchange’s lending product.

The companies plan to bring Mercado Bitcoin’s tokenized real-world assets to Sui and are exploring a connection with Hashi, Sui’s Bitcoin orchestration layer. Exploration of that integration should not be described as a completed Bitcoin lending launch.

The announcement provides the intended scope. It does not supply a single verified usage figure showing how many customers have already adopted every component of the partnership.

Distribution and settlement solve different problems

Making an asset available through a familiar platform can reduce the number of steps a customer must navigate. It may connect a local payment method, an exchange account and an onchain transfer inside one service relationship.

Settlement infrastructure then determines how the asset moves after it reaches the blockchain. A fast transfer does not by itself remove account checks, conversion costs or the conditions attached to receiving funds at the other end.

This distinction is useful when comparing payment propositions. The total customer experience includes the first conversion, the blockchain movement and the final use of the money. Improving one stage can be meaningful without making every stage immediate or free.

Collateral eligibility is a separate product decision

A token becoming acceptable as collateral does not mean a lender values it without limits. The amount that can be borrowed depends on the lender’s rules, the asset’s valuation and the conditions under which a position can be liquidated.

A customer also needs to distinguish the stablecoin’s own backing and redemption terms from the credit terms of the loan. A token designed to track a currency can still be used inside a lending arrangement with variable costs and liquidation risk.

Those are general features of collateralized finance, not evidence that this particular integration has encountered a problem. They explain why a product launch is most informative when it includes the actual borrowing and custody terms alongside the list of supported assets.

Tokenized assets need legal rights as well as a network

Bringing an investment instrument onto a blockchain changes how records and transfers can be handled. It does not automatically determine the holder’s claim against the underlying issuer, who may buy it or how cash flows reach the investor.

That makes distribution permissions, asset documentation and servicing arrangements central to the next stage of the partnership. The technically available token and the legally accessible investment may have different boundaries.

Sui’s official publication archive places the announcement alongside its broader financial infrastructure work, but the commercial test remains specific: functioning products, clear eligibility and observable use.

The partnership gives Sui a route into an established customer relationship in Brazil. Its eventual significance will depend on how much of the roadmap becomes available and whether customers use the resulting services repeatedly. The announcement establishes that direction; it does not yet demonstrate the scale of adoption.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: THORChain halts swaps after block reorg bug, slowing Binance hackers
summary: THORChain node operators paused swaps involving assets on 10 networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Tron.
content:
THORChain halted swaps across multiple blockchains on Saturday after an Ethereum block reorganization exposed a refund bug, which may have inadvertently slowed the movement of funds stolen from Binance, according to Chainalysis.

According to THORChain, the incident began at 11:34 UTC on Saturday, when a one-block reorganization on Ethereum removed a 10 ETH deposit that THORChain had already credited. When the swap failed to meet its price limit, THORChain issued a refund against funds the vault had never received. The sender’s actual deposit was also refunded, resulting in an extra 10 ETH payout, which then triggered an automatic pause. 

An Ethereum block reorganization, or reorg, happens when the network replaces a recent block with a competing block. The newly discovered flaw lets THORChain refund a payment that Ethereum no longer recognizes as having happened. A malicious actor could potentially exploit that mismatch.

“Now that this is public knowledge, every time there is a block re-org on an external chain, a malicious actor could perform a new transaction with the same nonce and would be paid funds by the THORChain vaults,” the protocol’s team said. 

THORChain node operators paused swaps involving assets on 10 networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Tron, while trading continued on Avalanche, Base and XRP, according to the protocol’s network status page. 

“Nodes will decide to re-enable chains as they are deemed safe,” said THORChain. 

Emergency pause delays Binance hackers’ fund movements 

The trading halt also disrupted attempts by North Korean hackers to launder funds stolen in last week’s $6.3 billion Binance hack, according to Chainalysis. 

“THORChain just inadvertently delayed the laundering of a significant amount of funds stolen from Binance,” said Chainalysis on Sunday, explaining the emergency pause is “preventing all users, including DPRK’s money launderers, from using cross-chain swaps.” 

“Until the service comes back online, neither the hackers nor anyone else can swap through a majority of THORChain’s bridges,” said Chainalysis. 

The disruption came as US authorities pressed crypto infrastructure providers to restrict the movement of stolen funds. 

On Saturday, the FBI urged THORChain node operators, DeFi services and other virtual asset providers to block transactions associated with addresses used by TraderTraitor to launder proceeds from the Binance hack. 

Related: THORChain’s RUNE jumps 13% after Binance’s record $6.3B hack

North Korean hackers have used THORChain to permissionlessly swap cryptocurrencies following previous attacks.

However, THORChain has continued to defend its role as neutral, permissionless infrastructure amid scrutiny over stolen funds moving through the protocol. 

In its third-quarter report, the project said it maintained that position despite pressure to block transactions linked to hacked funds.

THORChain founder John-Paul Thorbjornsen separately defended the protocol’s commitment to permissionless transactions, warning against shutting it down in response to pressure over illicit funds. 

“IMO if THORNodes decided to take the protocol offline next week then the experiment is over,” he said.

“The last bastion of unencumbered and neutral settlement is over. There will simply be no other venue and the protocol would have failed.”

title: Blackrock, JPMorgan and Visa Bolster Grayscale’s Crypto Growth Case
summary: Grayscale points to tokenized funds and stablecoin payments as evidence that crypto is becoming embedded in mainstream finance. Its research chief argues that institutional adoption should help sustain the industry’s progress regardless of the U.S. midterm election outcome. Blackrock and JPMorgan Ex...
content:
Grayscale points to tokenized funds and stablecoin payments as evidence that crypto is becoming embedded in mainstream finance. Its research chief argues that institutional adoption should help sustain the industry’s progress regardless of the U.S. midterm election outcome.

Key Takeaways

  • Blackrock and JPMorgan are expanding access to tokenized investment funds.
  • Visa’s annualized stablecoin settlement volume surpassed $25 billion.
  • Grayscale estimates 80%-85% of global crypto activity occurs overseas.

Blackrock and JPMorgan Expand Tokenized Fund Access

Blackrock, JPMorgan, and Visa are embedding digital assets in mainstream finance, bolstering crypto’s prospects regardless of the U.S. midterm election outcome, Grayscale argued on Oct. 28. Zach Pandl, head of research at the digital asset manager, cited those companies alongside Franklin Templeton, Mastercard, Fiserv, and Stripe as examples supporting his assessment of institutional crypto adoption. He wrote:

“Crypto is institutional. Public blockchain technology is now more deeply embedded into the mainstream financial system, facilitated by institutional adoption.”

Eligible European investors gained access to blockchain-based versions of existing cash-management strategies through Blackrock’s (NYSE: BLK) European tokenized fund share classes on Aug. 4. The offering uses Kinexys, JPMorgan’s blockchain business, to issue and manage digital fund shares on Ethereum. Official ownership records remain maintained through the funds’ transfer agent infrastructure.

The asset manager’s cash business also introduced two tokenized money market products in August, extending its offerings into digital markets. One added a tokenized share class to an existing fund; the other targeted digitally native institutional investors. Their potential uses include managing reserves that support payment stablecoins.

JPMorgan Chase’s (NYSE: JPM) asset management business expanded tokenized money market funds to Solana on Oct. 22. Its MONY private fund serves qualified investors, while JLTXX is a registered government money market fund designed to support stablecoin issuers’ reserve needs. Both are accessible through Morgan Money.

Visa’s Stablecoin Settlement Surpasses $25 Billion Run Rate

Payment networks are also expanding blockchain services, with Visa (NYSE: V) reporting newer adoption figures during its Oct. 27 earnings call. Chief Executive Officer Ryan McInerney said annualized stablecoin settlement volume had surpassed $25 billion, up tenfold year over year. The network supported 10 blockchains.

That expansion followed Visa’s April 29 announcement that its stablecoin settlement pilot supported nine blockchains and had reached a $7 billion annualized run rate. At that pace, settlement volume over 12 months would total $7 billion. The pilot gave participants more networks for settling obligations.

Commercial applications now include using stablecoins in payments and settlement to fund cross-border transfers outside traditional banking windows. Visa Direct’s stablecoin prefunding entered commercial production Oct. 15 through Inyo Global. That service lets eligible businesses fund payouts with USDC in near real time.

A separate seven-day trial involving Lloyds Banking Group demonstrated settlement between institutions across private and public blockchain environments. Lloyds used USDC to settle $750,000 in payment obligations with Visa. Funds reached Visa in under an hour, including during the weekend.

Global Demand and Bipartisan Support Broaden Crypto’s Outlook

International demand and bipartisan participation also underpin the assessment, although Pandl acknowledged that elections can affect crypto at the margin. Grayscale estimates that 80%-85% of global activity occurs overseas.

“Regardless of the outcome of the US midterms, users around the world will continue to seek out alternatives to fiat currencies as well as more effective payment systems, and foreign regulators will continue to put in place rules to support digital assets innovation in their jurisdictions,” Pandl stated.

Domestic support includes bipartisan passage of the GENIUS Act, a U.S. law establishing a payment stablecoin framework covering reserves, redemptions, and disclosures. Pandl also cited cross-party crypto participation and earlier congressional votes during the Biden administration. He wrote:

“Perhaps most importantly, federal government debt will likely continue to grow unchecked regardless of the makeup of Congress, driving investors to alternative stores of value including cryptocurrencies.”

title: XRP Ledger Reviews Two Token-Authorization Fixes Ahead of Any Validator Vote
summary: Two open XRP Ledger proposals address authorization checks for liquidity-pool tokens and existing trust-line balances. The changes remain under review and are not active network rules.
content:
TL;DR: Two open XRP Ledger proposals address authorization checks for liquidity-pool tokens and existing trust-line balances. The changes remain under review and are not active network rules.

XRP Ledger developers are reviewing targeted changes to the way issued-token permissions are checked in payment and liquidity-pool operations. The current public code record shows two relevant open proposals, both introduced on October 27.

The work is associated with the planned fixCleanup3_5_0 amendment. It should be described as protocol development, rather than a completed upgrade or evidence that ordinary XRP transfers now require issuer approval.

Pool tokens can carry exposure to two assets

The first open proposal, number 8648, would require an account acquiring a liquidity-provider token to satisfy authorization requirements for both assets in the corresponding automated market maker.

The reasoning follows the economic position. A pool token represents a claim connected to the pool’s assets. Checking only the direct deposit route may leave other ways to acquire the same exposure, including a transfer or exchange offer.

The proposal seeks consistency across those routes. That is relevant to an issuer using permission controls because a restriction needs to hold across the ways an account can obtain exposure, not simply at the most obvious entry point.

An existing balance should not create an exemption

The second open proposal, number 8650, addresses a payment-engine check that previously applied when an unauthorized trust line had a zero balance. The proposed behavior would prevent an existing unauthorized balance from being increased through further receipts.

The code discussion distinguishes receiving an issuer’s tokens from returning an obligation in the other direction. That distinction matters: preventing a new unauthorized holding need not prevent a legitimate redemption or remediation path.

Two broader proposals linked in the discussion are closed. Reading the current open changes is therefore more reliable than treating an earlier description of four proposed fixes as the final package.

Code review comes before activation

The XRP Ledger’s amendment documentation explains that changes affecting transaction processing must first be included in software and then receive sustained validator support. The stated threshold is more than 80% support for two weeks.

An open pull request has not completed that process. Review can alter the design, a release can include or defer it, and validators can make their own activation decisions. None of those stages should be collapsed into a claim that a rule is already enforced on mainnet.

For application developers, this means testing proposed behavior separately from the assumptions used in production. An anticipated error response is not necessarily the response a live transaction will receive today.

The impact is on issued assets and integration logic

These proposals concern permissioned issued-token relationships and claims on liquidity pools. They do not turn the native XRP asset into an issuer-controlled token. Keeping those categories clear avoids a misleading impression of a network-wide identity check on all holders.

The most useful preparation for affected integrations is to map the paths through which a customer receives a restricted asset, then identify how the application displays authorization failures and redemption options. A technically correct rejection can still confuse users if the interface presents it as an unexplained transaction error.

The development record does not by itself establish that an outside attacker exploited the paths under review. It establishes a proposed tightening of protocol behavior.

The next meaningful milestones are the merged implementation, its inclusion in a release and actual amendment status. Until then, the story is about improving consistency in permission controls, with the final scope still subject to review.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Ripple CEO Sees XRP as Institutional Gold Standard Within 5 Years
summary: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse sees XRP continuing to emerge as the institutional gold standard for crypto rails over the next five years. David Schwartz envisions mass retail adoption, with blockchain supporting how people manage money, receive payments, invest, lend, and borrow. Garlinghouse and Sch...
content:
1. News
  2. Market Updates
  3. Ripple CEO Sees XRP as Institutional Gold Standard Within 5 Years

Published:Nov 1, 2026, 7:30 PM EST

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse sees XRP continuing to emerge as the institutional gold standard for crypto rails over the next five years. David Schwartz envisions mass retail adoption, with blockchain supporting how people manage money, receive payments, invest, lend, and borrow.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 1, 2026, 7:30 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Ripple would prioritize XRP where it suited customer transactions.
  • Schwartz envisioned blockchain becoming as accessible as the internet.
  • Garlinghouse hoped to move 1% to 3% of transaction activity onchain next year.

Garlinghouse and Schwartz Outline XRP’s 5-Year Future

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse and board member and CTO emeritus David Schwartz outlined their five-year XRP outlooks in a video taken at Swell, shared on Oct. 28. Asked where he saw XRP and Ripple in five years, Garlinghouse answered:

“I think XRP … will continue to break out as the institutional gold standard for crypto rails.”

His answer followed an explanation of Ripple’s expansion from payments into corporate treasury and prime brokerage, with XRP serving as foundational technology. Garlinghouse said Ripple would prioritize XRP wherever it made sense, while recognizing that some transactions were better suited to fiat currencies or Ripple’s stablecoin, RLUSD. He preferred XRP handling a small percentage of a customer’s transactions over none.

Schwartz responded to the same five-year question by predicting mass retail adoption, comparing blockchain’s future accessibility with the internet. He described its potential role in everyday financial activity:

“It will be how they manage their money. It will be how they get paid. It will be how they invest. It will be how they lend and borrow.”

The discussion also connected tokenized real-world assets (RWAs) with the path toward broader retail adoption. That theme extended Schwartz’s June comments about XRP applications across financial services, including payments, tokenization, decentralized finance, and interoperability.

XRP Remains Central to Ripple’s Expansion

Garlinghouse expanded on the relationship between XRP and Ripple USD (RLUSD) in a separate Oct. 28 Bloomberg interview, describing XRP as “at the heart of everything Ripple does.” Discussing XRP’s role across Ripple, he explained that RLUSD complemented XRP, with roughly half of the stablecoin issued on the XRP Ledger. He said that activity brought liquidity and transaction volume to the network.

The assets addressed different needs within that strategy. Asked what XRP could do that RLUSD could not, he described its use as “a bridge asset between different currency pairs,” arguing that dollar-denominated stablecoins did not address every currency corridor in the same way. Ripple’s institutional XRP custody and payments extended access alongside its stablecoin services.

During his Oct. 28 Swell remarks, Garlinghouse reinforced that complementary relationship while reaffirming his commitment to the XRP ecosystem. He stressed:

“We will never give up on XRP.”

Transaction Growth Expands the Onchain Opportunity

In the video shared Oct. 28, Garlinghouse described transaction growth as an expanding opportunity for XRP, even as he expressed a preference for stronger crypto markets. Ripple’s products enabled more than $16 trillion in transactions during 2025, the company disclosed in its Oct. 28 update. It also projected a $900 million annualized product revenue run rate by year-end.

Corporate treasury illustrated how Ripple was incorporating digital assets into established financial workflows. Its RLUSD corporate cash management expansion included 24/7 Returns, through which eligible customers could earn returns on qualifying digital assets, including RLUSD held in a Ripple wallet. Participation remained subject to program requirements.

Garlinghouse said 99.9% of the $16 trillion in transactions still used traditional rails. He hoped to return the following year and report that 1%, 2%, or 3% had moved onchain, emphasizing: “Those are massive numbers to move onchain.”

About the author

WRITTEN BYKevin Helms

Kevin Helms is a cryptocurrency journalist specializing in Bitcoin, blockchain regulation, and global digital asset markets.

title: Polymarket Sets $3.9M Refund Plan After Third-Party Script Compromise
summary: Polymarket says its October 29 incident involved a compromised monitoring script. Its October 30 update put total refunds at $3.9 million, including losses linked to the trading pause.
content:
TL;DR: Polymarket says its October 29 incident involved a compromised monitoring script. Its October 30 update put total refunds at $3.9 million, including losses linked to the trading pause.

Polymarket has published a more detailed account of the third-party compromise that disrupted its international platform on October 29. The update shifts the focus from whether trading had reopened to how the attack worked and how customers would be compensated.

The company’s explanation is also a reminder that an onchain application can depend on offchain website components with access to active user sessions.

The refund figure includes more than drained funds

In its October 30 postmortem, Polymarket said it was returning $3.9 million: $2.7 million associated with the attack and another $1.2 million for pause-related losses. It reported that 95% of affected wallets had been refunded in full as of that afternoon.

The company said a compromised performance-monitoring script used some active sessions to sell positions and move funds. Its response included removing the script, clearing caches, resetting sessions and temporarily stopping trading and relayer activity.

The 95% figure is a timestamped company report. It should not be presented as a live refund completion rate or as proof that every disputed customer amount has been resolved.

Website code can become part of the financial boundary

A third-party script runs because a website chooses to load it. Depending on its permissions and execution environment, that script may interact with parts of the page and the browser session that users associate with the trusted application.

Mozilla’s documentation on subresource integrity describes one defense: a browser can compare a downloaded resource against an expected cryptographic hash and refuse content that does not match. It helps separate an approved file from a changed file served through the same address.

That mechanism is useful but limited. It does not decide whether the approved code was safe, and an application still needs a sound process for reviewing updates and controlling which resources are permitted to run.

A trading pause can create a second category of loss

In a market tied to a time-sensitive outcome, stopping transactions can affect users even if their wallet was never directly drained. A position might settle during the outage, or its market value might change before trading resumes.

Compensation for those effects requires a defined reference point. An operator needs to determine the relevant timestamp, position size and valuation method, then apply the same approach consistently. Otherwise, a refund headline can conceal disagreement about which losses are included.

This is particularly important when forced sales interact with thin liquidity. The difference between a displayed quotation and an executable price can become material precisely when the platform is under stress.

The durable test is the replacement control system

Removing the malicious file closes the immediate route described in the postmortem. The longer-term question is how future code changes are verified, what privileges external scripts retain and how quickly unusual activity is detected.

There is a sensible hierarchy here. Preventing an unnecessary script from reaching a sensitive page is different from detecting bad behavior after it has already begun. Both can be useful, but they should not be treated as interchangeable protections.

Users and counterparties will also benefit from clear reconciliation of completed refunds and any remaining disputes. An incident can be operationally resolved while accounting work continues.

Polymarket’s update provides concrete information about those separate tasks. The next assessment should focus on verified compensation outcomes and the effectiveness of revised controls, without assuming that blockchain settlement alone protects a user from every component of the application used to reach it.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Lumia – Why AI Agents Could Become the Biggest Owners of Real-World Assets
summary: Michael Huynh is Chief Marketing Officer at Lumia, a blockchain built specifically for tokenized real-world assets. It aims to handle an asset’s whole lifecycle, from compliant issuance to on-chain liquidity. Michael has worked full-time in crypto marketing since 2017, with Polygon, Avalanche and a ...
content:
Skip to content

Michael Huynh is Chief Marketing Officer at Lumia, a blockchain built specifically for tokenized real-world assets. It aims to handle an asset’s whole lifecycle, from compliant issuance to on-chain liquidity. Michael has worked full-time in crypto marketing since 2017, with Polygon, Avalanche and a few hundred other projects. He also co-founded the DCENTRAL conference series, which ran events across the US and into Asia.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Most of the RWA conversation so far has been about putting Treasuries on-chain and trading price exposure to gold. Michael argues that this barely scratches the surface; by his estimate, only about five percent of the opportunity has been unlocked. His real estate example shows what he means. Tokenizing a house is the easy part. The hard part is everything underneath it: deed settlement, county records, property taxes. Once those are bundled into the asset, mortgages and home equity lines of credit can follow it on-chain. The same reasoning turns tokenized gold from a trading instrument into a way for a mine to finance its next production run. That breadth is how Lumia positions itself against specialists like Ondo. Michael concedes they will win their chosen verticals, while Lumia tries to cover all the asset classes nobody has taken on yet.

The bigger bet is on the United States, and Michael is candid about what that costs. Lumia says it is deliberately building its US rails before the law arrives. He compares it to a racehorse that stays at the gate rather than wandering off to other tracks. The company has assembled a bipartisan bench of former Congressmen, including Tim Ryan and David McIntosh, with Gibson Dunn as counsel. The timing is pointed: the CLARITY Act failed a 49–50 cloture vote in the Senate in September. Michael says the stall was expected and that the US is still the market that matters, noting that institutions like BlackRock do not commit to a market without a path forward. He also explains LGP-01, which Lumia’s community passed with 95 percent support in early October. It retires the HyperNode program through a USDT buyback of future rewards and redirects the recovered tokens into a foundation fund for growth. He presents it as removing a structure that did not fit what institutional and government partners need.

The most provocative part of the conversation is about AI agents. Michael predicts, echoing Animoca Brands’ Yat Siu, that agents will become the largest holders of tokenized assets. He describes agents that score an asset against its listed price before buying, which speeds up price discovery. They would also source deals and send owners a daily summary, all within whatever permissions and spending limits the owner sets. A self-driving taxi that earns income around the clock is his example of an RWA category that does not exist on-chain yet. In the hot take round, Michael keeps at least half his heart with Bitcoin. He says agents combined with RWAs could take blockchain daily active users from one million to fifty million. He also sketches a ten-year future of reputation-based agent networks and “agentic billionaires”, and names The 100 as his favorite science fiction show.

title: Binance net outflows surge to $5.8B as withdrawals resume after record hack
summary: The exchange says withdrawals surged after some services resumed but have since slowed, with the outflows representing a fraction of its roughly $171 billion in customer assets.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 1, 2026

The exchange says withdrawals surged after some services resumed but have since slowed, with the outflows representing a fraction of its roughly $171 billion in customer assets.

Binance has recorded $5.8 billion in net outflows over the past 24 hours as customers withdraw funds following the exchange’s record $6.3 billion hack, according to data from DefiLlama. 

Binance said it began restoring withdrawals at 6:00 UTC on Sunday. By 3:30 UTC, it had processed $4.6 billion in withdrawals against $1 billion in deposits, resulting in net outflows of $3.6 billion.

Separate data from DefiLlama showed $5.8 billion in net outflows over the preceding 24 hours, as funds continued leaving the exchange after its initial update.

Binance said withdrawals initially surged but have since slowed and are stabilizing. The exchange noted that the outflows represented a small portion of the approximately $171 billion in assets it holds. Cointelegraph reached out to Binance for comment but did not receive an immediate response. 

The flows offered an early test of customer confidence following the $6.3 billion hack against Binance, the largest crypto theft on record. 

Related: Binance says phase one of withdrawals opens after $6.3B hack

Binance’s latest update at 12:36 UTC shows it enabled withdrawals for tokens across 15 networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and XRP Ledger, adding that it will continue to restore additional assets and networks in phases. 

Early data shared by Binance shows that the largest share of withdrawals were in USDt (USDT), followed by USDC (USDC) and Bitcoin (BTC). 

On Saturday, Binance said it had replaced 90% of the assets lost in the $6.3 billion hack using funds from its corporate treasury, its Secure Asset Fund for Users and its futures insurance fund.
