title: Only 40 Crypto Firms Survive Brazil’s Strict Licensing Deadline
summary: Reports indicate that after the October 30 deadline, out of the 150-200 companies expected, only 40 applied for operating licenses. The licensing process has consolidated the VASP industry, with many companies exiting Brazil as compliance requirements and costs ramp up. Around 40 Companies Applied t...
content:
1. News
  2. Regulation & Legal
  3. Only 40 Crypto Firms Survive Brazil's Strict Licensing Deadline

Published:Nov 1, 2026, 6:30 PM EST

Reports indicate that after the October 30 deadline, out of the 150-200 companies expected, only 40 applied for operating licenses. The licensing process has consolidated the VASP industry, with many companies exiting Brazil as compliance requirements and costs ramp up.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 1, 2026, 6:30 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Only 40 of 200 crypto firms met Brazil’s licensing deadline, forcing most to wind down operations.
  • Costly daily reporting rules forced out small firms, leaving larger players to supply crypto infrastructure.
  • Starting Nov. 6, banks will block transactions for unlicensed crypto firms, severing their fiat access.

Around 40 Companies Applied to Continue to Operate as VASPs in Brazil

The period established by the Central Bank of Brazil for virtual asset service providers (VASPs) to submit a request to continue operating in the country has finished, and the balance indicates that a majority of firms decided to exit the market.

According to local reports, of the expected 150 to 200 crypto firms, only around 40 applied to continue to operate and comply with central bank regulations, consolidating the service provider ecosystem.

Companies that completed and filed their applications will continue operating while the bank reviews their applications, while firms that did not apply will have a month from the October 30 deadline to wind down their activities and exit the market in an orderly manner.

While more companies might apply to become licensed and operate in Brazil, the central bank will have up to 2 years to respond to any application, making any attempt to enter Brazil a long process for any company not present today.

Tiago Severo, the crypto authority at Panucci, Severo e Nebias Advogados (PSNA), a Brazilian law firm, said the low number of firms applying is not only explained by the high capital requirements, but also by costs of complying with the reporting schedule the new framework establishes.

Severo told Livecoins that now, each company “must send custody of each client to the Central Bank every day and proof of reserves every month, have three years of audited balance sheets and a money laundering prevention program capable of undergoing audit.” “Many smaller platforms concluded they couldn’t sustain this,” he assessed.

Nonetheless, larger firms like Binance and Itaú did file applications, meaning customer capital will be custodied by companies with larger security budgets, which would result in better security protocols in practice.

For Severo, these larger firms will serve as infrastructure and service providers to smaller companies, which will rely on them to offer crypto services to their customers. “Medium-sized banks, cooperatives, and retailers will be able to offer crypto without setting up an exchange by hiring an authorized provider. The central legal question becomes who provides the regulated service and who responds to the customer,” he explained.

Starting on November 6, banks and payment providers will not be able to facilitate transactions for VASPs outside the regulatory regime, effectively crippling their ability to reach Brazilian customers using the legacy fiat system.

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: Billions flee Binance on reopen, THORChain founder opposes coin freeze: Hodler’s Digest
summary: Binance has reopened withdrawals following the world’s biggest ever hack, and THORChain co-founder argues it should not halt the protocol to comply with FBI demands.
content:
Binance reopens withdrawals

Binance has reopened withdrawals for 15 blockchain networks, after $6.3 billion was stolen by North Korean hackers from its hot wallets late last week.

Binance said today it had processed around $4.65 billion in withdrawals after reopening and received $1 billion in deposits. Founder Changpeng Zhao said that in the first 12 hours there had only been a 2.1% net outflow and that “98% choose to stay!”

DeFi Llama’s Binance wallet tracker shows $5.8 billion in outflows over 24 hours, however its figures may include internal transfers or movements into new hot wallets.

About 95% of the stolen crypto has already been replenished, using a mixture of Binance’s corporate reserves, insurance and 50% of the funds in the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).

The biggest hack in history happened on Thursday, when North Korea’s TraderTraitor group gained access to delegated wallet permissions via a compromised laptop. Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph that attackers could have stolen the funds without using EIP-7702 (account abstraction), but it may have helped them bypass safeguards and drain assets in one sweep.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng rejected the idea the hack could be attributed to a single compromised laptop.

“To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single ‘one-click’ action,” he said. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.”

FBI and Secret Service swoop in to help save billions

Zhao thanked the Secret Service today for “acting within minutes to help track and freeze stolen funds... your speed, expertise and dedication helped contain the damage.”

Elliptic estimated that about $2.84 billion of the stolen assets, mostly USDC and USDT, had been frozen on chain leaving the hackers with $3.33 billion. The attacker raced against time to beat the unprecedented stablecoin blocks by borrowing about $44.6 million of ETH against stablecoins on Aave.

The FBI attributed blame for the attack to the TraderTraitor hackers, which is associated with North Korea’s Lazarus Group and were also blamed for multibillion hacks of Bybit and Bitget. President Donald Trump indicated “we’ll talk to North Korea about it.” The FBI also released a list of addresses connected to the hack and pointedly singled out THORnode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other digital asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses.

Source: CZ

THORChain founder rejects freeze request

The North Korean hackers have used THORChain to permissionlessly swap cryptocurrencies following previous attacks, and the price of the protocol’s native token RUNE jumped 13% in expectation of all those fees.

Unfortunately for TraderTraitor, nine chains on THORChain, including Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tron on THORChain, are currently halted after automated systems paused the protocol for unrelated reasons on October 31.

Source: Vadim

According to THORChain developer Chad Barraford on the Unchained podcast, only around 50 or so individuals operate the 100 THORChain nodes. If the node operators refuse to halt the protocol or block addresses, as seems likely based on past incidents and public statements, they could face prosecution given the scale of the thefts and the involvement of the FBI and Secret Service.

THORChain founder JP Thor (who claims he is no longer involved) argued strongly that THORNode operators should not cooperate and should remain true to the ideals of decentralization and permissionlessness. “IMO if THORNodes decided to take the protocol offline next week then the experiment is over,” he said.

“The last bastion of unencumbered and neutral settlement is over. There will simply be no other venue and the protocol would have failed.”

If one third plus one of THORnode operators vote in favor they can halt activity. Nodes can also leave the network if they do not wish to process the funds. THORChain can operate with as few as four nodes processing transactions.

Lookonchain reports the attackers have also been using cross chain platform Relay to swap about half of $95.9 million of stolen SOL into Bitcoin.

Source: JP Thor

Ramifications of the hack

Crypto related stocks including Coinbase, Circle and Strategy sold off sharply following the hack, and crypto markets took a dive. But Strive CEO Matt Cole commented on Friday that Bitcoin had held up better than expected.

“I do have conviction that over any reasonable time frame, this does not change the investment thesis on Bitcoin,” Cole said. Bitcoin bottomed out around $76.5K and had recovered to 77,745 at the time of writing.
In the wake of the attack, Nasdaq-listed firm Next Technology Holding announced its board has approved selling off its 5833 Bitcoin Treasury worth around $450 million.

The attackers have reportedly amassed at least 18,000 Bitcoin and 430,000 Ether from the theft and subsequent swaps, although some tallies of the funds in the addresses identified by the FBI put the tally much higher at 551,612 ETH and 18,270 BTC. There are concerns that if those currencies are sold off quickly, that it would put downward pressure on BTC and ETH prices.

Meanwhile, Senator Cynthia Lummis and The Digital Chamber both used the hack to again push for crypto legislation to help prevent and mitigate the effects of future attacks.

Tampered Trezor linked to CryptoBilis reseller

Trezor has urged customers who bought its hardware wallets from former authorized reseller CryptoBilis since March to move their funds after a report of a suspected implant in a Safe 5 device. 

Trezor said Friday that a customer in Indonesia reported an unauthorized circuit board inside a Trezor Safe 5 bought on Tokopedia in August. Trezor said it had not yet examined the device and had received no reports of related losses.

The warning follows reports of crypto losses involving Ledger wallets sold through CryptoBilis that surfaced on Oct. 9. Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in one device.

Winners and Losers

At the end of the week, Bitcoin (BTC) is down 3% to trade at $77,745, Ethereum (ETH) is down 3.5% to trade at $2,260 and XRP (XRP) is down 3.9% to $1.02. The total market cap is at $2.21 trillion according to CoinMarketCap.

Among the biggest 100 cryptocurrencies, the top three altcoin winners of the week are Hyperliquid (HYPE) with a 13.7% gain, Midnight (NIGHT) on 12.6%, and Pepe (PEPE) on 12.6%.

The top three altcoin losers of the week are Curve DAO (CRV) which was down 18.6%, VeChain (VET) down 15.9% and Worldcoin down 13.8%.

Prediction of the Week

Binance hack could accelerate shift to DEXs: Standard Chartered

Standard Chartered’s Geoffrey Kendrick said one big winner from the hack was likely to be decentralized exchanges and reaffirmed his conviction in Uniswap and the UNI token.

“The decentralized exchange [Uniswap] has never had any exploits, and the hack of the largest centralized exchange, in Binance, should see the ratio of DEX to CEX trading continue to increase.”

The ratio is currently around 23.5%. Kendrick said he retains his $100 price target for Uniswap (UNI) for 2030. He said the Binance hack is “another reason why that forecast may end up being too low.”

Top FUD of the Week

CFTC chair warns of AI Agents dangers

CFTC chair Mike Selig says autonomous AI agents could challenge financial rules built around human traders, and regulators need to adapt. Selig said Super Intelligence (SI) could give smaller traders and businesses access to risk-management that was once reserved for larger institutions.

“SI can help process the vast amount of information significantly faster than human brain power and with greater accuracy,” he said.

But greater autonomy also comes with new risks. Agents could react unexpectedly to market conditions, while those using similar models could generate correlated trading behavior. The speed of autonomous transactions could also complicate market surveillance and risk management, he said.

Blockchain investigator Chainalysis hit by cybersecurity incident

Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis said it was targeted in a cybersecurity incident, similar to those suffered recently by other platforms.

“Based on the investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to investigation content, authentication credentials, or session tokens,” it said in a blog post on Friday. Some non-sensitive customer data was exposed, including user IDs, names and email addresses.

Chainalysis said it was using large language models to review its security and added the incident was not related to the recent crypto theft at Binance.

Texas brothers sentenced to 15 years in prison for armed crypto robbery

Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced to 180 months and 186 months in prison, respectively, for their armed robbery of cryptocurrency and kidnapping of a family in Grant, Minnesota.

The brothers were sentenced on Thursday before US District Judge Donovan W. Frank, according to a Friday news release. They had pleaded guilty in June.

On Sept. 19, 2025, the brothers, who had traveled from Texas to Minnesota, kidnapped Victim 1 and his family in their home at gunpoint, court documents said. They zip‑tied the family at gunpoint and held them for more than nine hours, demanding access to Victim 1’s cryptocurrency accounts.

Top Magazine Features of the Week

Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?

In typical Bitcoin style, the number one cryptocurrency turns 18 amid AI-driven security threats, quantum fears and the biggest exchange hack in crypto history.

Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

Attackers raced to convert stolen stablecoins into crypto that issuers could not freeze as industry players like Tether and Circle moved to immobilize billions of dollars in assets.

Will gold’s ‘infinite mint bug’ make Bitcoin more valuable?

A US fusion startup says it has turned mercury into gold. Could a potential increase in the gold supply strengthen Bitcoin’s claim to be a better form of digital gold?

title: KuCoin Announces Russia and Belarus Exit With Individual Account Deadlines
summary: KuCoin says it is discontinuing all services for users in Russia and Belarus. Affected accounts will receive their own deadlines for closing positions and withdrawing assets.
content:
TL;DR: KuCoin says it is discontinuing all services for users in Russia and Belarus. Affected accounts will receive their own deadlines for closing positions and withdrawing assets.

KuCoin has announced an immediate end to services for users in Russia and Belarus, while saying it will provide an orderly process for affected customers to close positions and withdraw assets. The October 29 notice applies across the exchange’s products and features.

The announcement leaves an important operational detail at account level. It does not publish one universal withdrawal deadline, so users should not assume a date circulating elsewhere applies to their circumstances.

The restriction covers the whole platform

KuCoin’s official notice attributes the decision to applicable legal and regulatory requirements. It says affected customers will receive notifications containing closure instructions and relevant deadlines. Customers who have not received a notification are told that no action is required on the basis of this notice.

The statement does not identify one particular enforcement order as the sole trigger. It should therefore not be expanded into a claim that a named government compelled the exit unless further documentation establishes that connection.

The published decision is nevertheless broad: the withdrawal from the two markets is not limited to a particular token listing or an individual trading product.

Closing exposure is different from transferring a balance

An account can contain more than assets that are immediately available to send elsewhere. A trader may have open orders, borrowed funds or positions that need to be closed before the remaining balance can be withdrawn. The exact procedure depends on the product and the account’s state.

That is why account-specific instructions matter. A simple transfer deadline would not explain how to deal with every possible obligation. It also would not identify which assets or networks remain available during a wind-down.

Customers should use the official account channel to establish those details. The exchange’s terms of use provide the wider contractual context, but a general terms page is not a substitute for the notification governing a particular closure.

Global brands still operate through regional boundaries

A blockchain transaction can cross borders without changing its basic technical format. An exchange’s relationship with a customer is different. Access depends on the legal entities, services and jurisdictional restrictions under which that relationship operates.

This creates a practical difference between ownership of a token and access to one venue that supports it. Losing access to a platform does not itself change the token’s network rules, but it can change how a customer trades, converts or withdraws that holding.

For businesses integrating exchange services, jurisdiction checks cannot be a one-time onboarding exercise. A later restriction can affect treasury operations, recurring transfers and the availability of a previously convenient source of liquidity.

Clear notices matter during an exchange exit

An orderly closure should make the remaining steps understandable: which positions must be settled, which transfers can still be requested and how exceptions are handled. Ambiguity can turn a manageable deadline into a rushed operational decision.

It can also create an opening for impersonators. KuCoin’s announcement specifically directs users to official channels. A message offering to accelerate an account exit should not be trusted merely because it references the real withdrawal from Russia and Belarus.

The relevant next evidence is the implementation of the closure process. The notice establishes the policy; account communications establish the individual timetable. Until those are read together, it would be misleading to describe every affected user as already unable to retrieve funds or to promise that all accounts will follow the same path.

For market observers, the story is another example of access risk at the service layer. The underlying assets can remain transferable while a particular commercial gateway changes the countries it serves.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin Mining Revenue Hits 11-Month High Despite Brutal Hashprice Decline
summary: While bitcoin prices have tumbled in the aftermath of the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack, miners closed October with their highest monthly revenue since November 2025. However, the leading crypto asset’s recent price deterioration has taken a considerable toll on mining profitability, with curren...
content:
1. News
  2. Mining
  3. Bitcoin Mining Revenue Hits 11-Month High Despite Brutal Hashprice Decline

Published:Nov 1, 2026, 5:30 PM EST

While bitcoin prices have tumbled in the aftermath of the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack, miners closed October with their highest monthly revenue since November 2025. However, the leading crypto asset’s recent price deterioration has taken a considerable toll on mining profitability, with current hashprice figures sitting 17.54% below their levels just 30 days earlier.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 1, 2026, 5:30 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin miners face mounting pressure as market conditions deteriorate.
  • October’s mining figures reveal an unexpected financial contradiction.
  • November could expose deeper vulnerabilities across the mining industry.

Bitcoin Mining Hashprice Slides 17.54% as Profit Margins Tighten

Bitcoin hashprice is a mining profitability metric that measures the estimated daily revenue generated per unit of computational power, typically expressed in U.S. dollars or satoshis per terahash or petahash per day.

On Oct. 1, 2026, each petahash per second (PH/s) of mining power generated an estimated $40.24 in daily revenue, but that figure has since dwindled to $33.18 as of Nov. 1, according to data from hashrateindex.com. The 17.54% decline is closely linked to the Binance hack and the subsequent market turmoil that battered bitcoin prices.

Despite the revenue slide, the network’s overall computational power stands at 1082.24 exahash per second (EH/s) and average block times are around 9 minutes 52 seconds. The broader cryptocurrency market downturn has yet to significantly impede mining operations, although increasingly compressed profit margins could eventually test miners’ financial resilience.

October Mining Revenue Hits $1.215 Billion Despite Bitcoin’s Market Decline

Amid these headwinds and bitcoin’s price logging a 7.3% decline in October, miners nevertheless recorded their most lucrative month since November 2025. According to monthly mining revenue records from newhedge.io covering the past 12 months, miners collectively generated $1.215 billion between Oct. 1 and Oct. 31.

November 2025 logged a total of $1.26 billion and the following month, in December 2025, miners logged around $1.20 billion. The fact is, crypto exchange security failures primarily unsettle market sentiment, erode liquidity and weaken investor confidence, yet they leave Bitcoin’s predetermined block issuance schedule entirely intact.

Mining economics, meanwhile, follow a predictable cyclical pattern: deteriorating hashprice pushes inefficient machinery out of operation, subsequent difficulty adjustments alleviate financial pressure, and the remaining miners secure a larger proportion of block rewards.

The deeper concern for bitcoin mining is not whether the industry can withstand another market shock, but how much financial punishment operators can absorb before their business models become untenable. October proved financially rewarding for bitcoin miners, but November could tell an entirely different story.

About the author

WRITTEN BYJamie RedmanNews Lead

Jamie Redman is the News Lead at Bitcoin.com News and a financial technology journalist based in Massachusetts.

title: HTX Ends UK Activity as FCA Secures Court Undertakings on Crypto Promotions
summary: The FCA says HTX is no longer active in the UK following a settlement over financial promotions. The agreement does not constitute an admission of wrongdoing.
content:
TL;DR: The FCA says HTX is no longer active in the UK following a settlement over financial promotions. The agreement does not constitute an admission of wrongdoing.

The Financial Conduct Authority says HTX has ceased UK activity after a settlement in litigation over cryptoasset promotions. The October 29 announcement describes restrictions on attracting new UK users and accepting deposits, with existing customers directed to the exchange’s official arrangements for residual assets.

The outcome shows why an exchange’s global availability and its ability to serve a particular jurisdiction need to be assessed separately.

The settlement changes the customer relationship

In its announcement, the FCA said it had secured High Court undertakings that HTX would not knowingly promote cryptoasset services unlawfully to UK consumers. New UK customers cannot register, and deposits are no longer available.

The regulator said HTX would not target, solicit or actively seek UK consumers. It also made clear that the settlement does not constitute an admission of liability or wrongdoing by Huobi Global or another person or entity.

That qualification matters. A negotiated restriction and an admission of the regulator’s allegations are different legal outcomes, even when the commercial result is a withdrawal from a market.

The proceedings have a longer history

The FCA’s published proceedings page records a sequence of court documents, beginning with the October 2025 claim and extending through the October 2026 orders. It provides the procedural background behind the latest announcement.

This is relevant because enforcement against an overseas platform is rarely a single action. Identifying defendants, serving proceedings and obtaining effective restrictions can involve several stages.

For other crypto businesses, the operational implication is that jurisdictional controls need to be reflected in more than the wording of a disclaimer. Marketing channels, onboarding systems and service access all form part of the practical customer relationship.

A platform also needs consistent information across those channels. A registration screen that rejects an applicant while a promotion still invites that same customer to join creates avoidable confusion. The practical task is to align the messages, account permissions and support responses so that the legal restriction has an intelligible effect for the people encountering it.

Permission checks need to match the service

The FCA’s warning page for HTX gives the regulator’s view of the firm’s permission status and the limitations on UK consumer protections. A recognizable exchange brand should not be treated as evidence that every service it offers carries the same safeguards in every country.

Even where a business has some form of registration, the scope matters. A permission for one activity does not necessarily cover another, and a registration entry is not a general guarantee of asset recovery.

For consumers, the most useful check is therefore the exact legal entity, the activity being offered and the relevant regulator’s current record, rather than a broad claim that a group is regulated somewhere.

Residual balances are a separate operational issue

Closing a market to new business and handling existing customer assets are distinct tasks. Customers need accurate information about the arrangements applicable to their own accounts, including any service limitations or deadlines.

The FCA directs UK users to HTX’s published information. That is more reliable than assuming that a general headline creates an identical withdrawal procedure for every account. The announcement itself does not provide a universal deadline or promise of instant processing.

The wider significance is a clearer boundary around the UK business. For the exchange, the next measure of an orderly exit is how consistently it implements the restrictions and communicates with affected users. For the industry, the case illustrates that operating across borders does not make local promotion rules irrelevant.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Crypto Weekly: Binance Hack Deepens Crypto Rout as Market Cap Falls to $2.7T
summary: The cryptocurrency market ended October down 10%, with its total capitalization falling from $3 trillion to $2.7 trillion amid widespread losses. Bitcoin declined 3.3% in the final week, extending its year-to-date losses to 11%, while ethereum fell more than 15% over 30 days. Pre-Hack Weakness The c...
content:
The cryptocurrency market ended October down 10%, with its total capitalization falling from $3 trillion to $2.7 trillion amid widespread losses. Bitcoin declined 3.3% in the final week, extending its year-to-date losses to 11%, while ethereum fell more than 15% over 30 days.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin ended October down 7.5% as the Binance hack deepened its downtrend.
  • Ethereum lost over 15% in 30 days, while Solana and Cardano fell 7% and 6.6%, respectively, in one week.
  • Bitcoin’s worst October since 2014 raises concerns about a potential continuation of losses in November

Pre-Hack Weakness

The cryptocurrency economy shed tens of billions of dollars in the final week of October, ending the month down 10% from its opening market capitalization of $3 trillion. The decline was particularly unusual given October’s historical reputation as a strong month for cryptocurrencies, including bitcoin.

According to seven-day data from Coingecko, bitcoin, which came close to reclaiming its year-opening price on Oct. 6, ended the final week of the month down 3.3%. The decline pushed the cryptocurrency’s year-to-date losses to 11%, effectively reversing an upward trend that began in August.

While a sell-off triggered by the Binance hack pushed bitcoin to nearly two-month lows, the cryptocurrency was already struggling. Prior to the breach, bitcoin had dropped over 7% after failing to clear the $87,000 resistance level in the first week of the month. As reported by Bitcoin.com News, this was bitcoin’s weakest October performance since 2014 and its first back-to-back October loss since 2011–2012, sparking concerns over its November outlook.

October was equally challenging for altcoins, with ether (ETH), the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, suffering even steeper losses. Like bitcoin, ETH rallied during the first week of October as the broader cryptocurrency market appeared to sustain September’s momentum. However, after briefly surpassing $2,700, ETH began a steady decline, falling to $2,300 by Oct. 29.

The sell-off following the Binance hack pushed ETH below $2,190 before a relief rally lifted it back above $2,200. Consequently, ETH ended the week down nearly 4%, extending its 30-day losses to more than 15%.

Other major altcoins, including solana (SOL) and cardano (ADA), suffered even steeper weekly declines, falling 7% and 6.6%, respectively. Many other altcoins recorded seven-day losses ranging from 3% to 4%.

Despite the broader downturn, a handful of altcoins managed to post weekly gains. Hyperliquid’s HYPE token, which came close to surpassing its all-time high on Oct. 29, ended the week up 13.6%, while zcash (ZEC) gained 0.6%. LEO, QNT and UNI also posted gains of 4.6%, 2.5% and 2.3%, respectively.

However, losses across bitcoin and numerous large-cap altcoins weighed heavily on the broader market, dragging the cryptocurrency economy’s total market capitalization from $2.8 trillion on Oct. 25 to $2.7 trillion by Nov. 1.

title: SEC Charges BG Wealth and DSJ Exchange Over Alleged $130M Crypto Scheme
summary: The SEC alleges BG Wealth and DSJ Exchange raised more than $130 million using false filings and trading claims. The civil complaint is an allegation, not a final judgment.
content:
TL;DR: The SEC alleges BG Wealth and DSJ Exchange raised more than $130 million using false filings and trading claims. The civil complaint is an allegation, not a final judgment.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission has brought a civil case against BG Wealth Sharing and DSJ Exchange, alleging that the businesses used official-looking filings to help sell an investment program built around purported crypto trading signals.

An October 30 litigation release details the complaint filed on October 29. The case puts a familiar distinction at its center: appearing in a government database does not mean a regulator has approved an investment.

What the SEC alleges

According to the SEC’s litigation release, the defendants raised more than $130 million from tens of thousands of retail investors. The regulator alleges that false Form ADV and Form D filings were presented as evidence of legitimacy, alongside promises of extraordinary, risk-free trading returns.

The SEC says neither entity was registered with it. It is seeking remedies including injunctions, disgorgement and civil penalties. The disputed filings have been removed from the Commission’s website, according to the release.

These are allegations in civil proceedings. The announcement does not establish a final court finding, a criminal conviction or a confirmed recovery amount for investors.

A filing is not an endorsement

The SEC’s guidance on false registration claims warns that the appearance of an entity or document in its systems can be used to mislead the public. The important question is what the particular filing actually means, rather than whether a screenshot bears a familiar logo.

A notice submitted by a business can contain information supplied by that business. It is not automatically a regulator’s independent assessment of solvency, trading performance or the safety of customer assets.

That distinction becomes especially important when a promoter uses a real database link to support a much broader claim about licensing or approval.

The identity behind the document matters as much as the document itself. A filing for one entity does not validate another business with a similar name. Nor does a registration claim explain who holds customer funds. Comparing the contracting entity, payment recipient and service provider can expose gaps that a polished presentation leaves out.

Trading signals can hide the basic investment questions

Sophisticated terminology can make a proposition sound more precise without making its economics clearer. Investors still need to understand who controls the money, how returns are generated, what losses are possible and how withdrawals are funded.

A displayed account balance is also different from an independently verified asset. If a platform controls both the dashboard and the explanation of returns, apparent consistency on a screen is weak evidence that the underlying activity occurred.

The SEC separately maintains an alert on misuse of exempt reporting adviser filings. Its relevance is practical: a technically authentic filing can still be used to create a misleading overall impression.

The case now turns on evidence and remedies

The legal process will determine how the allegations are resolved and what remedies, if any, are ordered. Even when a regulator seeks repayment, the amount ultimately available can depend on locating assets, establishing claims and completing the relevant proceedings.

For readers following the case, verified court developments will be more useful than claims circulating through former investor groups. A complaint, an asset restraint and a distribution to victims are separate milestones.

The wider lesson is specific rather than technological. Crypto trading language, automated signals and public filings do not remove the need to examine the legal entity and the investment mechanism. The SEC’s case challenges whether those signals of legitimacy were used to conceal the absence of the protections investors believed they had.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: CZ Praises US Authorities for Halting $6B Binance Hack Fallout
summary: The co-founder and former CEO of Binance praised the role U.S. law enforcement agencies played in handling the aftermath of the over $6 billion hack the exchange suffered at the hands of North Korean hackers, crediting them with keeping the market afloat. CZ Praises US Role in Binance Hack Aftermath...
content:
The co-founder and former CEO of Binance praised the role U.S. law enforcement agencies played in handling the aftermath of the over $6 billion hack the exchange suffered at the hands of North Korean hackers, crediting them with keeping the market afloat.

Key Takeaways

  • CZ praised U.S. agencies like the FBI for tracking and freezing funds after Binance’s $6B security breach.
  • This swift law enforcement response prevented a deeper bitcoin market crash despite $1.5B in liquidations.
  • Wall Street analysts dismissed long-term impacts, blaming the exchange’s security rather than Bitcoin’s code.

CZ Praises US Role in Binance Hack Aftermath

As Binance continues to recover from the security incident that caused losses of over $6 billion, Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, better known as CZ, has highlighted the role of US law enforcement agencies in mitigating the hack’s impact on the wider cryptocurrency market.

Zhao, one of the first voices linked to the exchange to acknowledge that the strange movements did “look like a hack on Binance,” praised the agencies’ role in collaborating to contain the scope of the incident.

“US Law Enforcement agencies (FBI, USSS, IRS and more) provided vital help in this incident, including tracking, freezing, etc.,” Zhao said on social media channels after the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the hack to a North Korean hacking group known as Tradertraitor.

Furthermore, the former Binance executive stressed that the hack’s impact on cryptocurrency prices was contained by the agencies’ swift actions.

“A tweet can’t fully express our gratitude. Many crypto bros may not realize, a lot of the ‘why bitcoin didn’t drop more?’ credit goes to them,” Zhao assessed.

While bitcoin dropped to a multi-week low shortly after the hack, reaching $76,320 and sparking over $1.5 billion in liquidations, and larger crypto shares like Coinbase and Strategy fell, for CZ, this might have been worse without the involvement of these agencies.

Specifically, the FBI has been actively involved in tracking the movement of stolen funds across the blockchain, calling on private sector entities to block transactions involving these stolen funds, and publishing a list of ETH, BTC, and SOL addresses that hold or have held assets from the theft and are operated by or closely connected to North Korean Tradertraitor actors.

Wall Street firms have downplayed the hack’s effect on bitcoin prices, with analysts from Cantor-Fitzgerald and TD Cowen pointing out that the hack revealed weaknesses in Binance’s security infrastructure and not in Bitcoin’s solid programming.

While painful, analysts agreed that Bitcoin’s long-term direction was unfazed, and that prices would eventually recover, with Bitwise’s CIO Matt Hougan predicting prices would return to prior levels within a week.

title: Strategy Reports 848,517 Bitcoin as Q3 Gains Put Cash Coverage in Focus
summary: Strategy reported 848,517 BTC as of October 25 and large third-quarter digital-asset gains. Cash coverage and financing obligations remain central to assessing the results.
content:
TL;DR: Strategy reported 848,517 BTC as of October 25 and large third-quarter digital-asset gains. Cash coverage and financing obligations remain central to assessing the results.

Strategy’s latest results show how far its financial profile has moved beyond the size of its Bitcoin holdings. The company reported 848,517 BTC as of October 25, alongside a quarter in which digital-asset valuation gains dominated operating income.

The October 29 release also emphasized dollar liquidity and the obligations attached to its financing securities. Together, those figures offer a more useful picture than a single profit number.

Bitcoin valuation drove the earnings headline

Strategy’s third-quarter announcement reported $20.91 billion of gains on digital assets and approximately the same amount of operating income. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $19.12 billion, with diluted earnings of $44.75 per share.

The company also reported $5.07 billion of USD assets and described those assets as covering 3.4 years of dividend and interest obligations on its stated measure. These are company-reported figures with different measurement purposes.

The holdings snapshot is dated October 25. It should not be silently treated as a live wallet balance or substituted for the September 30 financial reporting date.

An accounting gain is different from spendable cash

When the market value of an asset rises, the resulting accounting gain can increase reported income even if the asset has not been sold. That does not make the gain meaningless: it reflects a change in economic value. It does mean the income statement and cash position answer different questions.

Dividend payments, interest and operating bills ultimately require resources that can be delivered when due. A strong quarter for a treasury asset may therefore coexist with a need to manage funding carefully.

The reverse also applies. A subsequent valuation decline can weigh on earnings without establishing that an immediate cash payment of the same size is required.

Comparisons across quarters should preserve that distinction. Stronger reported profit may reflect a larger asset position, a greater price increase, or both, without saying much about the underlying software operation. A useful review therefore separates changes in the quantity of Bitcoin, changes in its valuation and cash flows generated by the rest of the business.

The financing stack matters to common shareholders

Strategy’s business has to be assessed across the securities used to finance it. The SEC’s investor education material explains the general difference between common and preferred stock, including preferred shareholders’ usual priority over common shareholders for dividends and liquidation proceeds.

That ordering helps explain why gross Bitcoin value cannot be read directly as value available to common stockholders. Each layer can have its own payment rights, conversion provisions and sensitivity to market conditions.

New financing may increase the asset base while also changing the claims against it. The relevant comparison is the resulting position for each class of investor, including dilution and ongoing costs.

Liquidity coverage deserves a stress test

A coverage period is a useful starting point, but its assumptions deserve attention. It depends on which obligations are included, how liquid the supporting assets are and whether future commitments change. It is not a promise that every possible financing need has already been funded.

For investors, a practical reading of the quarter separates three questions: how much Bitcoin the company owns, how its securities distribute gains and risks, and how it meets cash commitments through different market conditions.

The latest figures make the scale of the treasury clear. They also reinforce why evaluating Strategy requires attention to cash and capital structure alongside Bitcoin conviction. A rising asset price can improve several measures at once, while still leaving those measures conceptually distinct.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Thorchain Glitch Blocks Binance Hack Route as FBI Presses Nodes
summary: A one-block Ethereum reorganization on Saturday triggered a double refund involving 10 ETH on Thorchain, setting off an emergency pause that disrupted cross-chain swaps across most of its supported networks. Chainalysis said the malfunction inadvertently delayed laundering activity connected to Bina...
content:
A one-block Ethereum reorganization on Saturday triggered a double refund involving 10 ETH on Thorchain, setting off an emergency pause that disrupted cross-chain swaps across most of its supported networks. Chainalysis said the malfunction inadvertently delayed laundering activity connected to Binance’s $6.4 billion theft. Meanwhile, the FBI urged Thorchain node operators to block transactions associated with North Korean hackers, creating an extraordinary collision between technical failure and law enforcement pressure.

Key Takeaways

  • A 10 ETH double refund triggered Thorchain’s emergency pause across 12 supported networks.
  • Chainalysis identified an unexpected obstacle to laundering funds stolen from Binance.
  • The FBI urged Thorchain operators to block transactions linked to North Korea’s Tradertraitor.

Ethereum Reorg Jolts Thorchain Into Emergency Shutdown

The trouble began when Ethereum reorganized a single block, effectively replacing a previously accepted segment of its transaction history. A 10 ETH deposit intended for a Thorchain vault appeared in the discarded block but never returned to Ethereum’s canonical chain. Thorchain’s observers had already recognized the deposit and credited the vault. When the associated swap failed its price conditions, the protocol refunded 10 ETH that the vault had never actually received.

Another deposit from the same wallet was subsequently refunded, leaving the vault approximately 10 ETH short. The discrepancy activated Thorchain’s automatic solvency protections, which halted its Ethereum processing. There was no evidence of malicious intent behind the transaction. Technical accounts attributed the incident to a collision between Ethereum’s reorganization and Thorchain’s deposit verification procedures.

Chainalysis Says Binance Hack Laundering Hit a Roadblock

The malfunction quickly snowballed into a broader operational disruption. Trading and new swaps stopped across 12 of Thorchain’s 13 supported external networks, although certain previously initiated outbound payments remained operational. Chainalysis seized on the irony, writing that Thorchain had “inadvertently delayed the laundering of a significant amount of funds stolen from Binance.”

Chainalysis added:

“One happened this morning and caused [Thorchain] to incorrectly issue a double refund to someone who had deposited 10 ETH. This triggered an ’emergency pause’ on [Thorchain], preventing all users, including DPRK’s money launderers, from using cross-chain swaps. Until the service comes back online, neither the hackers nor anyone else can swap through a majority of [Thorchain]’s bridges.”

The blockchain intelligence firm explained that the emergency pause prevented ordinary customers and suspected North Korean money launderers alike from accessing most of Thorchain’s cross-chain swapping routes. The disruption followed Binance’s Oct. 29 breach, which investigators attributed to North Korea’s Tradertraitor operation. Blockchain analysts had identified stolen funds moving through Thorchain-associated routes, including activity connected to earlier cryptocurrency thefts.

Yet the interruption was neither a targeted asset freeze nor a permanent blockade. Thorchain’s safeguards had reacted to an accounting problem, not the origin of incoming cryptocurrency.

FBI Presses Thorchain Node Operators to Block North Korean Funds

While developers investigated the malfunction, federal authorities were pursuing a separate approach. The FBI, working alongside the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, issued an Oct. 31 alert urging infrastructure providers to prevent transactions involving wallets connected to the Binance theft. Its appeal explicitly named Thorchain node operators, alongside RPC providers, instant exchanges, decentralized finance (DeFi) services and blockchain analytics firms.

The request was voluntary rather than a court order. It nevertheless placed fresh scrutiny on a permissionless protocol whose operators have previously resisted selective transaction blocking. Thorchain technical co-founder Chad Barraford responded that operators possessed publicly accessible information, describing the situation as “No subpoenas required, a best-case scenario for investigations.” His remarks addressed investigators’ access to information rather than whether operators would comply with the transaction-blocking request.

A 10 ETH Accounting Error Complicates a Multibillion-Dollar Heist

The episode exposed a peculiar contradiction in cross-chain infrastructure. A system designed to move cryptocurrency without centralized permission briefly became unavailable because its own accounting protections detected a missing deposit. Developers planned changes to observation and finalization procedures while addressing the affected vault’s shortfall. The interruption lasted several hours, with restoration proceeding across individual chains.

The FBI’s request remained a separate matter. Even if Thorchain’s software safeguards can stop entire networks, selectively refusing transactions associated with particular wallets presents a different technical and governance problem. For a few hours, a misplaced 10 ETH accounting credit accomplished what a federal appeal had not demonstrably achieved: It shut a major swapping route to everyone, including suspected North Korean money launderers.

title: Next Technology Authorizes Sale or Pledge of 5,833 Bitcoin After Risk Review
summary: Next Technology has authorized selling or pledging its reported 5,833 BTC. The decision creates flexibility; it does not confirm that a transaction has occurred.
content:
TL;DR: Next Technology has authorized selling or pledging its reported 5,833 BTC. The decision creates flexibility; it does not confirm that a transaction has occurred.

Next Technology Holding has given management permission to reduce or finance its Bitcoin position after a board review of custody and market risks. The company reported approximately 5,833 BTC when announcing the decision on October 30.

For the wider market, the important distinction is between authorization and execution. A board can create the option to sell an asset without deciding when, at what price or through which counterparty a transaction will happen.

The board has approved several routes

The company’s announcement, distributed through GlobeNewswire, permits transactions in one or more tranches. The stated options include exchange sales, negotiated block trades and pledging Bitcoin to obtain financing.

Next Technology cited the recent Binance security incident and broader technological concerns in explaining the review. It specifically said none of its Bitcoin was held on or through Binance.

The release does not establish a completed disposal or a signed financing agreement. It also gives no assurance about the timing, price, amount or completion of a future transaction. Those qualifications belong at the center of any interpretation of the announcement.

A sale and a pledge have different consequences

Selling Bitcoin exchanges price exposure for cash. Once a sale settles, subsequent gains or losses on the disposed coins no longer accrue to the company. The trade-off depends on the price received and how the proceeds are used.

A pledge instead uses the coins as collateral. That can provide liquidity while retaining some economic exposure, but the borrower also takes on contractual obligations. Interest, collateral requirements, maturity and a lender’s enforcement rights can become as important as the asset’s market price.

Without those terms, it is impossible to treat a potential borrowing as equivalent to a sale, or to determine which route would leave shareholders with greater flexibility.

The sequence could matter too. A company might use financing to meet a near-term need and later reduce that borrowing through asset sales. Alternatively, it could sell only enough to fund a particular commitment. Neither sequence is announced here, but both illustrate why the full authorized balance should not be mistaken for a fixed disposal schedule.

The equity story extends beyond coin count

A corporate Bitcoin holding is only one part of an investment in the company that owns it. As Investor.gov explains, shares represent ownership in a business. They do not give each shareholder direct control of particular treasury assets.

The value reaching ordinary shareholders depends on liabilities, operating expenses, financing terms and the number of shares outstanding. A headline multiplying a reported coin balance by a market price therefore cannot settle the investment case.

Investors would need to know what restrictions already apply to the assets, whether proceeds are earmarked for specific commitments and how any financing changes the company’s overall capital structure.

Execution disclosures will carry more weight

The next meaningful development would be a disclosure identifying a completed sale, an executed pledge or a decision to retain the position. Price, quantity and resulting cash or debt balances would turn the board’s general authority into something that can be assessed.

The company’s reference to quantum computing is a statement of its risk considerations, not evidence that Bitcoin’s cryptography has been broken. A corporate risk review and a demonstrated technical exploit require different standards of proof.

Until transaction details emerge, treating all 5,833 BTC as immediate market supply would go beyond the announcement. The present news is that management has more options, with the consequences still dependent on what it actually does.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Binance Hacker Moves $96M in Stolen Solana to Bitcoin as Laundering Efforts Continue
summary: The attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance security breach has begun converting nearly $96 million worth of stolen Solana (SOL) into Bitcoin (BTC), according to on-chain tracking platform Lookonchain.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC SOL

The attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance security breach has begun converting nearly $96 million worth of stolen Solana (SOL) into Bitcoin (BTC), according to on-chain tracking platform Lookonchain.

On November 1, the wallet associated with the incident transferred approximately 486,970 SOL, valued at $46.4 million, toward Bitcoin through cross-chain service Relay Protocol.

The latest movement involves a reported stash of 970,522 SOL, worth approximately $95.9 million. The conversion marks another stage in the attacker’s efforts to move stolen cryptocurrency across blockchain networks, complicating efforts by exchanges and security firms to monitor and restrict the funds.

Binance Hacker Routes Stolen Solana Through Relay Protocol

Lookonchain identified the activity through an address labeled as belonging to the Binance attacker on Arkham Intelligence. Its November 1 post stated: “The Binance hacker is swapping the stolen 970,522 SOL ($95.9M) for BTC.”

Lookonchain reported that the hacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance-related breach is converting 970,522 stolen SOL, worth approximately $96 million, into Bitcoin. Source: @lookonchain via X

The 486,970 SOL transfer represents approximately half of the reported holdings. The remaining balance was valued at roughly $49.5 million at the time of the reported transactions. The figures describe the reported conversion pool and its initial movement, rather than a confirmed $95.9 million Bitcoin transfer completed in a single transaction.

Relay Protocol facilitates cross-chain cryptocurrency swaps by connecting users with different blockchain networks and liquidity sources. Its involvement provides another route for transferring assets between Solana and Bitcoin. However, the use of a cross-chain service does not automatically remove the transaction history or make the funds untraceable.

The latest conversion also follows earlier movements involving other stolen cryptocurrencies. Law enforcement officials have been monitoring the attacker’s wallet activity as investigators and blockchain intelligence companies work to identify transactions linked to the breach.

FBI Confirms North Korean Involvement in Binance Hack

The latest transactions come after the FBI formally attributed the October 29 Binance attack to North Korea’s state-sponsored cyber operation known as TraderTraitor. The agency announced its findings on October 31, confirming that North Korea was responsible for stealing more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from the exchange.

The FBI attributed the record $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance on October 29, 2026, to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking group, identifying it as the largest known crypto heist. Source: FBI Cyber Branch via X

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs had previously identified TraderTraitor as the group behind the incident. Its investigation estimated that approximately $6.36 billion in digital assets was transferred from Binance wallets across ten blockchain networks, with most of the withdrawals occurring within roughly 20 minutes.

The FBI also identified the hackers’ efforts to convert stolen assets, primarily into Ethereum. It warned that the attackers could move the funds through decentralized finance platforms and instant cryptocurrency swap services to facilitate additional laundering.

In its statement, the agency warned of “further laundering” through related technologies and urged cryptocurrency exchanges, blockchain operators, analytics companies, and other service providers to block transactions associated with the identified addresses.

The latest SOL-to-BTC activity adds another layer to those concerns. Although the FBI previously highlighted Ethereum conversions, the movement reported by Lookonchain shows that the attacker is also using cross-chain infrastructure to move assets into Bitcoin.

Binance Covers 95% of Stolen Assets as Withdrawals Resume

Binance has continued replenishing the assets affected by the security breach while coordinating with law enforcement and industry partners to trace the stolen funds.

On November 1, the exchange confirmed that it had covered approximately 95% of the affected amount, up from 90% in its October 31 recovery update. The remaining 5% consists of less-liquid tokens that may require additional time to acquire through market purchases and over-the-counter transactions.

Binance has expanded withdrawal services to include DOGE on its native network and ETH, USDT, and USDC on Optimism, following earlier resumptions across BTC, ETH, BSC, XRP, and Base. Source: Binance via X

The replenishment effort has involved the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a portion of the Futures Insurance Fund, and Binance’s corporate treasury. The exchange has repeatedly stated that customers will not bear the financial impact of the attack.

“Binance will absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds, not our users,” the company said in its security incident updates.

The exchange also began restoring withdrawal services in phases on November 1 after temporarily suspending withdrawals while conducting security reviews. The initial phase covered several networks and assets, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB, Solana, XRP, and Dogecoin. Binance said it would gradually restore additional services as security checks were completed.

The company separately reported that approximately $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen on-chain through coordination with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, asset issuers and other industry participants. This represents a separate enforcement and recovery effort from Binance’s own asset-replenishment commitment.

Bitcoin Conversion Complicates Crypto Recovery Efforts

Moving stolen cryptocurrency into Bitcoin can create additional challenges for investigators, particularly when transactions pass through multiple networks and wallet addresses.

Unlike centralized stablecoins, which issuers can freeze at the token-contract level, Bitcoin does not have a central authority capable of freezing funds across its network. However, this does not mean that Bitcoin transactions are anonymous or impossible to trace. Its public blockchain records transactions, allowing investigators and analytics firms to follow fund movements between addresses.

Cross-chain services can complicate that process by splitting transactions across different networks and liquidity providers. Investigators may need to connect activity across multiple blockchain records to establish where assets move after each conversion. Exchanges and other regulated service providers can also restrict deposits and withdrawals associated with identified addresses.

The FBI’s request for cryptocurrency businesses and infrastructure providers to block transactions linked to TraderTraitor reflects the importance of coordinated action in containing the movement of stolen assets. Binance has also credited industry partners for helping freeze funds and track transactions following the October 29 breach.

For now, the reported movement of nearly $46.4 million in Solana toward Bitcoin remains an important development in the ongoing investigation. Whether the attacker can move the entire $95.9 million pool into BTC remains to be established. Meanwhile, the combination of public blockchain monitoring, transaction screening, and cooperation among industry participants will remain central to efforts to trace the stolen funds and prevent further transfers.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto: The FBI said that North Korea was responsible for the theft of about $6.3 billion in digital assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance. Soon after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, some political and administration figures began offering their opinions with a US election approaching on Nov. 3 and voting already having begun in many locations. Coinbase led a selloff in crypto-linked stocks following Binance’s record-breaking $6.3 billion hack.

FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack

The FBI said that the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of about $6.3 billion in digital assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance on Thursday.

The FBI said on Saturday in a news release that it refers to this specific North Korean malicious cyber activity as “TraderTraitor,” which it has most recently observed converting stolen assets mostly into Ether (ETH). 

It expects these assets to be further converted, using DeFi and instant swap services, as the hackers move to more advanced laundering stages.

The FBI urged private sector entities including THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other digital asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets. A full list of addresses is provided on the news release.

Binance hack sparks pre-election political clashes 

Soon after the $6.3 billion hack of Binance, the biggest in crypto history, some political and administration figures began offering their opinions with a US election approaching on Nov. 3 and voting already having begun in many locations.

President Donald Trump was asked at a news conference on Friday about the hack of Binance. “We don’t know. We’re looking at that, the hack with Binance. They’re saying they’re going to get it back, they’re saying they’re guaranteeing it,” he replied.

The crypto exchange said in a post on X late Friday that it would cover any losses. “We want to be clear about our commitment: Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.” It added that about $3 billion of the stolen funds had already been frozen in various locations. On Saturday, Binance said it had already covered 90% of the impacted amount of the hacked loss.

It was not clear whether there was any immediate political advantage to be gained from the hack, which was widely attributed to a North Korean group, but Republican and Democratic sides began staking out positions almost immediately.

Coinbase leads crypto stock selloff following $6.3 billion Binance hack

Shares of publicly traded cryptocurrency companies fell sharply Friday, with Coinbase dropping more than 13% a day after reporting a decline in third-quarter revenue, as the industry dealt with Binance’s $6.3 billion hack.

Other crypto-linked stocks also declined, with stablecoin issuer Circle Internet Group (CRCL) falling more than 9% and Bitcoin treasury company Strategy (MSTR) dropping about 8%, according to Yahoo Finance data at the time of writing.

The selloff also hit Bitcoin mining and data center operator IREN (IREN), whose shares fell more than 10%, and blockchain-based financial services company Figure Technology Solutions (FIGR), which dropped about 9%.

The declines followed Thursday’s disclosure of the Binance breach. The exchange confirmed Friday that hackers stole about $6.3 billion in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.

title: DeepSeek developing AI agent requiring less human input: Report
summary: The proposal comes amid intense competition among AI developers, including US companies Anthropic and OpenAI, the SCMP said.
content:
The proposal comes amid intense competition among AI developers, including US companies Anthropic and OpenAI, the SCMP said.

Chinese artificial intelligence company DeepSeek has revealed a design to increase the autonomy of AI coding assistants so they can perform multiple tasks with less human intervention.

The aim is to reduce human input in coordinating and monitoring multiple AI agents, according to a paper published by the company’s DeepSeek Harness team and reported by Singapore’s South China Morning Post on Sunday.

Managing multiple agents demands human attention, the team said, noting that “single-task limits depend on model capabilities, while multitask limits depend on human attention.”

The DeepSeek paper said a person can oversee only three to five active AI agent sessions simultaneously. Its proposed system would distribute tasks among agents and coordinate their work, leaving humans free to review results and make decisions.

The proposal comes amid intense competition among AI developers, including US companies Anthropic and OpenAI, according to the SCMP.

Cointelegraph reported last October that Chinese artificial intelligence models were outperforming US counterparts in cryptocurrency trading, according to data from blockchain analytics platform CoinGlass.

AI chatbot DeepSeek led a crypto trading experiment, being the only AI model to generate a positive unrealized return of 9.1%. The results surprised crypto traders, given that DeepSeek was developed at a fraction of the cost of its US rivals.

title: Binance says phase one of withdrawals opens after $6.3B hack
summary: The crypto exchange said it has begun phased withdrawals after the record hack the FBI has blamed on North Korea.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 1, 2026

The crypto exchange said it has begun phased withdrawals after the record hack the FBI has blamed on North Korea.

Binance said it has reopened its Bitcoin network in phase one of resuming withdrawals after a major hack of about $6.3 billion in funds.

The crypto exchange had suspended user withdrawals after the attack on Thursday, which the FBI blamed on North Korean operatives.

“First batch network now opened in phase one of withdrawals is $BTC bitcoin network,” Binance said on X.

In an earlier X announcement on Sunday, Binance had said it would roll out withdrawal services in phases, which will be progressively available. Updates will be available on its official X channel, it added.

“We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand, so that each network and asset pair can be restored carefully, with stability and security checks completed before access is reopened,” Binance said.

Users should check the withdrawal page for their selected asset and network, or visit the Binance network status page to confirm availability, the company said.

During the phased rollout, it is expected that there will be some congestion, longer processing times and even temporary delays, Binance said, so if a withdrawal is not successful, users should try again after a short while.

Cointelegraph reported on Saturday that Binance said it had replenished 90% of the assets stolen in the hack, up from 80% a day earlier, and remained on track to resume withdrawals Sunday.

North Korean defense spending supplemented

Related: Crypto losses from North Korea hackers in 2025 rose 51% YoY: Report

Those findings came from a CertiK report that attributed more than $2 billion of an estimated $3.4 billion in 2025 crypto security losses to groups tied North Korea, across 79 of 656 incidents documented that year.

As Cointelegraph reported, between 2016 and early 2026, North Korea-linked actors stole an estimated $6.75 billion in cryptocurrency across 263 documented incidents, according to CertiK, citing findings by independent onchain researcher Taylor Monahan.

title: Quant (QNT) Price Prediction: Bulls Target $302.67 Retest After Reclaiming $200 Support
summary: Quant (QNT) has regained the psychologically important $200 level, strengthening its technical position after a volatile October.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: QNT

Quant (QNT) has regained the psychologically important $200 level, strengthening its technical position after a volatile October.

The recovery comes as Quant price breaks above a falling wedge resistance on the 8-hour chart, putting several higher price targets back in focus.

The latest technical analysis identifies $238.28, $253.48, $275.11, and $302.67 as potential upside levels if the breakout receives confirmation. However, QNT still faces resistance from the Ichimoku cloud, while mixed momentum indicators suggest that further consolidation remains possible before a sustained upward move.

QNT Reclaims $200 as Falling Wedge Breakout Draws Attention

QNT was trading around $200–$201 on November 1, recovering from recent fluctuations that pushed the token toward the $192 area. Its 24-hour trading range extended approximately from $192 to $208, reflecting continued activity around the reclaimed psychological level.

QNT has broken above the falling wedge resistance on the 8-hour chart with strong volume. Source: DigitalChartist on TradingView

The recovery follows a volatile October, during which QNT traded within a broader range of approximately $175–$223. Market capitalization estimates ranged from $2.3 billion to $2.9 billion, while daily trading volume stood between roughly $57 million and $64 million across different market snapshots.

A technical chart shared by DigitalChartist on TradingView shows QNT breaking above the descending resistance of a falling wedge on the 8-hour timeframe. The breakout was accompanied by stronger trading volume, suggesting increased buying participation during the recovery.

However, the price is now approaching the Ichimoku cloud, an indicator commonly used to assess trend direction, support, and resistance. The cloud could present an additional obstacle before QNT establishes a stronger upward trend.

DigitalChartist’s analysis also identifies a possible retest of the broken wedge resistance. Such a move would allow the market to test whether the former resistance area can become support. A successful retest followed by a decisive move above the Ichimoku cloud would provide stronger technical confirmation.

The analyst’s projected upside levels are $238.28, $253.48, $275.11, and $302.67. These are conditional chart targets rather than confirmed price levels, with each depending on the continuation of the breakout structure.

QNT Price Prediction: Moving Averages Support the Broader Uptrend

QNT’s daily chart presents a constructive longer-term picture, although short-term momentum remains less decisive. The token is trading above most of its tracked moving averages, indicating that the broader recovery structure remains intact.

The 10-day simple moving average (SMA) is near $193, while the 10-day exponential moving average (EMA) sits around $196–$197. The 20-day SMA and EMA are also clustered near $196–$197, creating an important short-term support area.

Quant (QNT) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Further below, the 50-day moving averages are positioned around $177–$180. The 100-day averages range from approximately $120 to $143, while the 200-day averages sit between $95 and $114. The distance between the current price and these longer-term averages reflects the strength of QNT’s preceding advance.

The positioning of the 50-day average above the 200-day average also supports the intermediate bullish structure. However, moving averages are lagging indicators and cannot independently confirm that the recent breakout will continue.

Momentum oscillators offer a more balanced assessment. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) on the daily timeframe is hovering around 49–53, placing it near the midpoint of its range. This suggests that buying pressure has not reached an overbought condition, but neither has momentum established a decisive bullish advantage.

The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) readings are also mixed. Recent snapshots show the MACD line fluctuating around its signal line, with a negative histogram in some readings. This indicates that the short-term recovery still needs stronger momentum confirmation.

Bollinger Bands provide additional context. The middle band is positioned around $196–$197, while the upper band ranges from approximately $212 to $219. The lower band sits near $175–$179. QNT’s return above the middle band is constructive, although a move toward the upper band would require sustained buying interest.

Key QNT Support and Resistance Levels to Watch

The $200 level remains the central technical reference for QNT. Holding above it could improve market sentiment and provide a foundation for another attempt at nearby resistance.

Immediate support is concentrated between $192 and $197. This zone combines recent trading lows with the short-term moving-average cluster. A sustained move below this area could weaken the recovery and expose lower support levels.

QNT shows bullish momentum after breaking its local downtrend, retesting bull flag support, forming a double bottom near $175, and bouncing off the daily 50-day SMA. Source: @DrewDog12380 via X

The next support region lies between $182 and $189, where the 50-day moving averages and other technical reference levels converge. Below that, the $171–$176 region represents another important demand area, particularly given its relationship with October’s price action.

On the upside, QNT faces initial resistance between $201 and $208. A daily close above this range would strengthen the case for a move toward the $211–$216 area.

The next resistance cluster sits around $223–$226, representing a potential hurdle before the higher targets identified on the 8-hour chart become relevant.

Classic pivot calculations also place immediate resistance near $202, followed by a second resistance level around $212–$213. These levels broadly align with the short-term resistance zones identified through moving averages and recent price action.

A sustained recovery above $216 would improve the technical outlook. It could then open the way toward $238.28, followed by $253.48 and $275.11. The final projected target at $302.67 would require a much stronger continuation of the current upward structure.

Traders Identify $203.85 as an Important Breakout Level

Other market participants are monitoring additional resistance levels that could influence QNT’s next move.

Crypto trader @Ekoanalizz highlighted $203.85 as a key resistance level on the daily chart. The analysis suggests that a decisive breakout could attract additional buying interest and improve the prospects for bullish positions.

The daily QNT chart identifies $203.85 as key resistance, with a breakout potentially triggering a sharp rally and strengthening bullish momentum. Source: @Ekoanalizz via X

The level is particularly relevant because QNT has been consolidating near $200 beneath a descending trendline. The token’s October trading range, which extended roughly between $175 and $223, shows that buyers have yet to establish a sustained move above the broader resistance structure.

Another technical analysis shared by @DrewDog12380 identifies several bullish developments, including a break above a local downtrend, a potential bull flag retest, and a double-bottom formation near $175.

The chart also highlights a rebound from the daily 50-day simple moving average and a bullish RSI crossover. Declining volume during the pullback was identified as another potentially constructive signal, as it could indicate that selling pressure was easing.

That analysis marks upside projections near $312 and $992. However, these are considerably more aggressive than the $302.67 target identified in DigitalChartist’s 8-hour analysis. They should therefore be treated as separate technical scenarios rather than a unified market forecast.

The difference between these projections highlights the uncertainty surrounding QNT’s longer-term price trajectory. A breakout above immediate resistance would provide a clearer basis for evaluating higher targets.

Limited QNT Supply Adds Another Factor to the Market Outlook

Quant’s circulating supply is another factor frequently discussed by traders evaluating its price potential. Estimates cited in market commentary place the circulating supply at approximately 14.5 million QNT, although some traders refer to a figure closer to 12 million when discussing the token’s available float.

A relatively limited circulating supply can influence price movements when demand increases, particularly if available liquidity is thin. However, circulating supply alone does not guarantee a supply squeeze or higher prices. Exchange liquidity, trading volume, token distribution, and broader market conditions also influence price discovery.

At a market capitalization approaching $2.9 billion, QNT already represents a substantial crypto asset. Any sustained advance would therefore require sufficient capital inflows and continued demand rather than relying solely on its limited token supply.

The combination of a falling wedge breakout, a potential bull flag retest, and a recovery above the daily 50-day moving average has attracted bullish attention. Nevertheless, confirmation through price action and trading volume remains essential.

Looking Ahead: Can Quant Reach $302.67?

QNT’s recovery above $200 has improved its near-term technical structure, but the next resistance levels will determine whether the rebound develops into a sustained advance.

The immediate bullish scenario depends on the token maintaining support around $192–$197 and breaking above the $203.85 resistance highlighted by traders. A stronger move through $208 and the $211–$216 resistance cluster would provide additional confirmation.

QNT is retracing toward 100 EMA support, where a rebound could support a resumption of its short-term bullish trend. Source: TradingView

If buying pressure continues and QNT moves above the Ichimoku cloud on the 8-hour chart, the projected targets at $238.28, $253.48, and $275.11 could become relevant. A sustained advance beyond these levels would bring the $302.67 target into focus.

On the other hand, rejection near $203.85 or failure to maintain the $192–$197 support zone could extend the consolidation. A deeper correction may expose the $182–$189 region, followed by support around $171–$176.

For now, the technical picture remains cautiously constructive. QNT’s position above its longer-term moving averages supports the broader uptrend, while neutral daily oscillators indicate that the market has not yet established decisive short-term momentum.

The $200 level, the $203.85 resistance, and the Ichimoku cloud are therefore important areas to monitor as traders assess whether Quant can extend its recovery toward $302.67.
