title: Google AI Spending Shock: Alphabet Loses Over $500 Billion After Q3 Earnings Miss
summary: Alphabet shares plunged nearly 13% on October 29 after the Google parent reported third-quarter results below Wall Street forecasts, wiping roughly half a trillion dollars from its market value.
content:
Skip to content

Alphabet shares plunged nearly 13% on October 29 after the Google parent reported third-quarter results below Wall Street forecasts, wiping roughly half a trillion dollars from its market value.

The sell-off followed disappointing advertising revenue, slower Google Search growth, and rising concerns over the cost of its AI expansion. Despite strong Google Cloud performance, investors questioned whether Alphabet’s growing infrastructure investments could generate sufficient returns.

Alphabet Q3 Revenue Miss Raises Google Search Concerns

Alphabet reported third-quarter revenue of $127.6 billion, representing a 25% increase from $102.3 billion a year earlier. However, the result missed analysts’ expectations of approximately $128.2 billion, according to LSEG data.

Sundar Pichai reported Alphabet’s Q3 2026 revenue rose 25% year-over-year to $127.6 billion, driven by AI-led growth across its businesses. Source: Sundar Pichai via X

Google advertising revenue reached $82.01 billion, falling about $1.4 billion short of market estimates. Within that segment, Google Search and other advertising revenue increased 12% to $63.35 billion, compared with 17% growth in the previous quarter. YouTube advertising revenue also increased 9% to $11.2 billion.

The slowdown has drawn attention to Google’s expanding use of AI-powered search features. Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler indicated that increased adoption of AI Mode contributed to the deceleration in search advertising growth. The conversational interface encourages longer interactions, but those queries currently generate less advertising revenue per use than traditional search.

Foreign-exchange movements also affected the quarterly comparison. However, investors remain concerned about how Google’s transition toward AI-generated search experiences could affect its established advertising model.

The issue was highlighted by Dave Wagner, portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors. He said, “In a market worried about AI cannibalizing the franchise, investors need to see search accelerating, not decelerating.”

His comments reflect a central concern surrounding Alphabet’s AI strategy: maintaining search engagement while ensuring that new AI experiences continue to generate advertising revenue.

AI Infrastructure Spending Drives Negative Free Cash Flow

Alphabet’s increasing AI investment was another source of investor concern. The company recorded $51.4 billion in capital expenditure during the third quarter, with most of the spending directed toward technical infrastructure supporting AI development and cloud services.

Alphabet reported its first negative free cash flow in 22 years, reaching $9.07 billion as aggressive AI infrastructure investments drove heavy spending on data centers and cloud capacity. Source: Reuters via X

The investment contributed to negative free cash flow of approximately $9.07 billion, compared with a $5.9 billion deficit in the previous quarter. It marked the second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow and a significant change for a company that had historically generated substantial cash from its operations.

Alphabet’s management said the deficit reflected the cost of expanding technical infrastructure, alongside inventory accumulation for Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) systems and a $5.2 billion cash payment related to a European Commission fine.

The spending also coincided with a decline in reported earnings. Alphabet’s net income available to common shareholders fell 25% year over year to $26.17 billion. Diluted earnings per share came in at $2.12, while the company’s adjusted EPS was reported at $2.67, below the $3.02 analyst estimate.

An unrealized investment loss also affected the results. Alphabet reported negative $8.2 billion in other income and expenses, primarily because of a decline in the value of its SpaceX investment. The non-cash accounting loss reduced reported earnings but was separate from the company’s infrastructure expenditure.

Chief Financial Officer Anat Ashkenazi maintained Alphabet’s 2026 capital expenditure forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion. However, she told analysts that spending would increase significantly in 2027, without providing a specific figure.

This outlook has raised questions about how quickly the company’s AI investments can translate into additional earnings and sustainable cash generation.

Google Cloud Growth and Gemini AI Demand Offer Support

Despite the pressure on advertising, Google Cloud delivered one of Alphabet’s strongest quarterly performances. Revenue increased 103% year over year to $30.71 billion, supported by demand for AI infrastructure, enterprise services, and computing capacity.

Alphabet ($GOOGL) fell nearly 13% after missing Q3 2026 revenue and EPS estimates, as slowing search ad growth and investment losses weighed on investor sentiment. Source: @KobeissiLetter via X

Cloud operating income more than tripled to $11.1 billion, while its operating margin expanded to 36.2%, compared with 23.7% in the same quarter last year. Alphabet also reported a $561 billion cloud backlog, reflecting substantial contracted demand for its services.

The company’s AI products showed further growth. Alphabet’s first-party model APIs were processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, representing a 40% increase from the previous quarter. The Gemini app also reached one billion users, while the company introduced additional models through its Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon lineup.

CEO Sundar Pichai pointed to increased search engagement as evidence that the company’s AI investments were supporting product usage. He said the year-over-year Search query growth rate was “the highest it’s been in the last five years.”

These developments offer a different perspective from the market’s reaction. Google Cloud is benefiting from enterprise demand, while Gemini adoption and AI-powered search are expanding the company’s reach.

However, the immediate challenge remains monetization. Alphabet must demonstrate that increased AI usage can generate enough advertising and subscription revenue to justify the substantial costs of building and operating its infrastructure.

GOOG Technical Analysis: $280 Support in Focus

Alphabet’s Class C shares (NASDAQ: GOOG) closed at approximately $282.32 on October 29, down 12.29% during the session. The stock also traded near $278.29 at its intraday low, reflecting strong selling pressure following the earnings announcement.

Alphabet Inc (Google) Class C price chart. Source: TradingView

The decline pushed shares below several important short- and medium-term moving averages. TradingView’s technical indicators point to a bearish short-term structure, with downward-sloping averages reinforcing the recent selling pressure. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has also moved toward oversold territory.

However, an oversold RSI reading does not independently confirm a bullish reversal. Traders may look for stabilization and a confirmed recovery above nearby resistance before treating the decline as a potential trend change.

On the downside, the $275-$280 region represents an immediate support area. A sustained break below this zone could expose the stock to additional historical demand levels.

On the upside, the $290 level represents initial resistance, followed by the psychological $300 mark. A broader resistance region extends toward $328.50, where previously broken support levels could influence future price movements.

A sustained recovery above $300 would provide an early indication that selling pressure is easing. Until then, the technical structure remains under pressure, with buyers needing to defend the lower support region.

AI Investment Returns Remain Alphabet’s Biggest Test

Alphabet’s latest earnings highlight the growing gap between AI demand and the financial cost of meeting it. Google Cloud, Gemini, and AI infrastructure services are attracting customers, but the company is also committing increasingly large sums to data centers, servers, networking equipment, and custom processors.

The pressure could continue into 2027. Management has already indicated that capital expenditure will rise significantly, while greater use of third-party computing capacity could weigh on cloud margins in the near term.

For investors, the central question is whether AI can strengthen Google’s existing businesses without weakening the economics of traditional search advertising. Alphabet’s expanding cloud business offers an important source of growth, but its search operations remain critical to overall revenue generation.

The latest sell-off shows that investors are increasingly focused on the financial returns from AI rather than spending commitments and product launches alone. Alphabet’s ability to convert growing AI adoption into higher revenue, improved margins, and positive free cash flow could become an important factor in determining the stock’s next direction.

title: How Bitcoin Is Helping Reshape Online Slots
summary:
Bitcoin (BTC) is changing different aspects of handling money. Yet, online gaming platforms are one area you might not have come across. By looking at how the introduction of this
The post How Bitcoin Is Helping Reshape Online Slots appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Bitcoin (BTC) is changing different aspects of handling money. Yet, online gaming platforms are one area you might not have come across. By looking at how the introduction of this cryptocurrency and other digital assets has changed the scene, you can understand another way in which Bitcoin is causing a positive impact.

  • Instant Access to Games and Fast Withdrawals
  • Flexible Gaming Options With No Fiat Currency Worries

Instant Access to Games and Fast Withdrawals

The length of time taken for a transfer is one of the major issues with fiat currencies and traditional banking methods. In terms of online slot games, players have generally had to wait several days for withdrawals to reach their bank account or for a physical check to arrive.

When sending crypto funds to a gaming platform, deposits arrive almost instantly and withdrawals are processed rapidly by reputable gaming operators. By using the blockchain, the platform ensures that transfers go through very fast, without any need for banks or other middlemen to approve them. Other cryptos, such as Litecoin (LTC), Tron (TRX), and Cardano (ADA), are also commonly accepted, which gives players more choice and flexibility.

A Growing Player Base Reflected in More Themes and Features

The diverse range of games in this Bitcoin gaming platform confirms that this is a growing market. The slots section includes freshly released titles, covering themes as far-ranging as mythology, wild animals, and sports. They also have a variety of features, such as jackpots, bonus rounds, and free spins. The fact that players can sign up and fund their accounts so quickly has allowed this industry to reach out to a new audience, which is reflected in the games being released. Some of the games even use crypto imagery to make them stand out.

Classic slots featuring symbols like fruits and bells can also be played. The crypto aspect simply means that players can get started more quickly and receive any winnings without any delay. As BTC continues its move toward mainstream acceptance, there will be more people playing games in this way, which will lead to greater levels of demand for new slot themes and features.

Flexible Gaming Options With No Fiat Currency Worries

Using fiat currencies for online gaming was the only possible approach in the past, but it never fully suited the online approach to slots for many players. It could be argued that cryptos fit more naturally into the way that online slots have evolved, as they can be used for flexible gaming transactions.

This is particularly true for anyone who wants to avoid uncertainty with their local fiat currency. It’s no coincidence that Bitcoin and other digital assets have gained ground more rapidly in countries where the national currency has lacked stability and where inflation has been a major problem.

By using cryptos to access online slots, users avoid the risk of sticking to a currency that could rapidly lose value due to inflation. Bitcoin is known for its volatility, but it’s also worth taking into account that its entire mining process is based on the idea of the token being worth more over time, since it becomes increasingly difficult to mine through the halving process.

If you prefer a digital asset that retains the same value day after day, a stablecoin like Tether (USDT) is an option that gives you exactly that. Stablecoins are pegged to the value of a real-world asset. In the case of USDT, this is the US Dollar. So, one Tether is always worth $1. This removes a lot of the potential price fluctuations that might make online gaming transactions more volatile than you would like.

A More Private, Secure Approach

Finally, for many people, it’s the privacy and security of digital assets that make them a sound choice. These tokens allow you to send money anywhere in the world on a pseudonymous basis. The reason that most cryptos aren’t fully anonymous is that someone could theoretically track your transactions until they find one that reveals your identity, which is typically at the fiat on-ramp or off-ramp stage.

Despite this, a lot of people feel more comfortable using cryptos for their online gaming funds. It’s definitely more private than sending from your bank account or normal debit card. In this way, you add a layer of extra security to your online activity as well. The transparency of the blockchain and the high level of password security mean that it’s far more difficult for anyone to illegally access your funds. Privacy-focused tokens like Litecoin offer an even higher degree of privacy.

Since you need to send your funds from a self-custody wallet to your gaming account, it’s important that you choose the right type of wallet and then store the password details securely. Thankfully, there are now more user-friendly crypto wallet options than ever before.

The option of using crypto to access online slot games has made it easier for more people to play in this way, without having to learn all the details of blockchain technology.

title: SEC Charges Two Companies in $130 Million Crypto Trading Scheme
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

SEC Charges Two Companies in $130 Million Crypto Trading Scheme
The SEC has charged two companies with defrauding investors of over $130 million through a crypto Ponzi-like scheme.
This post SEC Charges Two Companies in $130 Million Crypto Trading Scheme first appeared on Bitcoin M...
content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission charged two foreign-operated, Colorado-incorporated companies with running a crypto investment fraud that used false federal filings to raise more than $130 million from tens of thousands of retail investors.

The defendants are BG Wealth Sharing Ltd. and DSJ Exchange Pty Ltd. A complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California alleges that from at least October 2025 through June 2026, the companies induced investors in more than 40 states and several U.S. territories to join a “wealth-sharing program.” 

Participants were promised risk-free returns generated by so-called signals for crypto asset trading.

According to the complaint, BG Wealth claimed to be the world’s largest hedge fund, claimed registration with the SEC as an investment adviser, and said it partnered with a licensed and secure crypto trading platform, DSJ Exchange. 

The SEC says none of those claims were true. The complaint alleges the companies submitted false Form ADV and Form D filings to the SEC. Those filings were viewable on the agency’s website and shared with investors as evidence that the SEC had licensed or approved the firms.

Laura D’Allaird, chief of the SEC Enforcement Division’s Cyber and Emerging Technologies Unit, described the operation in a statement. 

SEC: Crypto scheme was ‘a Ponzi-like tactic’

“This alleged scheme was well-planned,” she said, citing social media, encrypted messaging channels, weekly live videoconferences and a mobile app used to engage investors. The complaint alleges the defendants displayed fake certificates bearing the SEC’s seal and made periodic payments to some investors, “a Ponzi-like tactic,” while misappropriating the remaining funds.

The SEC charged both companies with violating the antifraud provisions of the Securities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

It charged BG Wealth with violating Sections 204(a) and 207 of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. The agency seeks permanent injunctions, disgorgement with prejudgment interest, and civil penalties against both companies, along with conduct-based injunctions against BG Wealth.

The Form ADV and Form D filings have been removed from the SEC website.

The SEC’s Office of Investor Education and Assistance has issued investor alerts warning that scammers are using exempt reporting adviser filings to create a false impression of legitimacy. The agency encourages investors to check the background of anyone offering or selling a crypto investment through Investor.gov.

The SEC said it received assistance from the Alberta Securities Commission, the Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, the Texas State Securities Board, the Utah Division of Securities, the Washington State Department of Financial Institutions, the Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions, and other authorities.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Blockchain Firms Link North Korea to $6.3 Billion Binance Hack
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Blockchain Firms Link North Korea to $6.3 Billion Binance Hack 
Chainalysis and TRM Labs have linked yesterday’s $6.3 billion Binance hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.
This post Blockchain Firms Link North Korea to $6.3 Billion Binance Hack  first appeared on Bitcoin Magaz...
content:
Blockchain analysis firms Chainalysis and TRM Labs have linked the $6.3 billion Binance hack yesterday to TraderTraitor, a unit associated with North Korea. If confirmed at this scale, the theft would be the largest crypto hack on record. 

Chainalysis puts the total at $6.4 billion in its own assessment. Chainalysis says funds began leaving Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains around 4:20 p.m. Eastern Time on October 29. 

The firm said the attacker used an operational wallet funded through Tornado Cash to submit signed authorizations that allowed a Binance hot wallet to run attacker-deployed code. 

The attacker then swept assets into addresses under its control. Binance has said its initial investigation points to a compromised engineer’s laptop, which gave an attacker access to a service container and enabled unauthorized withdrawals. 

The exchange said it has found no evidence of a wallet private key leak.

The attacker reportedly tried to outpace freezes by converting stablecoins into ether and other assets that issuers cannot freeze. Chainalysis said the attacker swapped $325 million in stablecoins into $285 million in ETH over roughly 20 minutes, then sent the remaining $175 million to stopover wallets. Freezes began by 5:14 p.m. Eastern, according to the firm.

Market reacts to the hack

Bitcoin dropped toward $76,000 on Friday morning before trading near $77,400. Other crypto followed suit and posted declines of their own. Total market liquidations reached $1.5 billion, with bitcoin accounting for $468 million and ether for $358 million. 

Long positions, which bet on higher prices, bore most of the losses. The sell-off coincided with a separate incident at decentralized betting platform Polymarket, which suspended international trading after hackers drained more than $2.6 million from user accounts.

Binance said Thursday that the security incident affected about $6.3 billion in assets, surpassing the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of 2025, which was attributed to North Korean hackers. Former CEO Changpeng Zhao wrote on X, “It does look like a hack.” Zhao no longer runs the exchange but remains a key shareholder.

Stablecoin issuers moved to contain the fallout. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company froze more than $1.567 billion in USDT and that protecting the industry and its partners is its main priority. 

Circle co-founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire said Circle froze more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. First Digital CEO Vincent Chok said FDUSD stolen in the attack has been frozen. Binance says about $3 billion has been frozen onchain in total.

Binance has enough funds to cover the incident

Binance says it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the incident. About $5 billion of that reserve is held in the same token assets that were affected, and the company is buying the remainder through market and OTC channels. 

The exchange says frozen and protected assets remain subject to verification and plans to publish an updated Proof of Reserves. 

Reuters, citing a person familiar with the matter, reported that Binance is working with the FBI and the U.S. Secret Service.

Bitcoin may have further downside

Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets research, Geoffrey Kendrick, wrote in an email to CoinDesk that the negative price action may have some way to go. He said a new base will form after assets are unfrozen and more details of the hack emerge. 

Kendrick argued that the incident could accelerate a shift toward decentralized exchanges. Chainalysis has warned that scammers are impersonating the firm, including those offering fund recovery and recruiting services. 

Victims should treat unsolicited recovery offers with caution and rely on official channels for updates.

At the time of writing, Bitcoin is trading near $76,700.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: How to Buy Bitcoin in 2026: 5 Platforms Compared for Beginners
summary:
Your first Bitcoin purchase should feel simple. A few early choices make that easier. Start by deciding how much effort you want to spend and what you plan to do
The post How to Buy Bitcoin in 2026: 5 Platforms Compared for Beginners  appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Your first Bitcoin purchase should feel simple. A few early choices make that easier. Start by deciding how much effort you want to spend and what you plan to do with the coins. Many beginners feel pressure to buy a large amount at once. A small first order lets you learn the process with little at stake.

  •       Ease of use. Look for a clear sign-up flow and a plain checkout screen. Beginner-friendly platforms show the price, the fee and the amount of Bitcoin you receive before you confirm. Customer support matters if something goes wrong.
  •       Payment options. Pick a platform that supports a payment method you already use. Bank transfers usually cost less. Cards and digital wallets are faster. A platform with several options gives you a fallback if one method fails.
  •       Fees. Costs come in several forms. A platform may charge a percentage fee, a spread built into the price, or both. Network fees apply when you withdraw to your own wallet. Beginners often focus on the headline fee and miss the spread. Always read the final quote.
  •       Speed. Instant payment methods usually deliver Bitcoin to your account within minutes. Bank transfers can take days. Moving coins to your own wallet depends on the Bitcoin network, where a first confirmation arrives in about 10 minutes on average. This overview of how Bitcoin mining works explains why.

Two more points deserve attention. Decide whether you want to keep Bitcoin on the platform or send it to a wallet you control. A guide to Bitcoin economics and network security covers the background. Then confirm that the service is available in your country and check what identity verification it asks for.

Here are five ways to get started.

  • 1. Paybis
  • 2. Cash App
  • 3. Strike
  • 4. River
  • 5. Bitpanda
  • Bitcoin Buying Platforms Compared: Fees, Payments, and Availability
  • Conclusion

1. Paybis

Paybis offers several ways to pay. Cards and PayPal are accepted, and bank transfers are available too. The platform serves customers in 180+ countries and lists 90+ cryptocurrencies. Beginners who already use PayPal can buy Bitcoin with PayPal, and the Paybis homepage covers the other options.

2. Cash App

Cash App offers Bitcoin purchases inside its money app. The minimum purchase is $1. Fees are tiered by order size. Cash App lists 2.0% for orders from $1 to $499 and 0% for orders of $2,000 or more. A spread of up to 0.75% may also apply to market buys, and it appears on the confirmation screen.

Auto Invest, which buys on a schedule, carries no fee. Standard withdrawals complete in 24 hours or less. The Bitcoin page refers to US states and territories. It also says Bitcoin services are not licensable in all of them, so check eligibility first.

3. Strike

Strike is an app that focuses on Bitcoin. You can fund purchases with a linked bank account or a wire transfer. Debit card purchases are available too. A single buy can range from $1 to $2.5 million.

Strike says its fees are as low as 0.49% and fall as your volume grows. You can schedule recurring buys to spread your purchases over time. For personal accounts, Strike waives recurring-buy fees after the first week. App availability and some features depend on your jurisdiction.

4. River

River is a platform that focuses on Bitcoin. Its fee page lists 1.00% on one-time orders up to $1 million. Direct deposit and recurring buys are listed at 0%. For recurring buys, the waiver starts seven days after the first order, and that first order carries the standard fee.

The minimum fee is $0.01, and a price spread may also apply. The fee page does not say which payment methods or countries are supported. Check both on the River website before you sign up.

5. Bitpanda

Bitpanda describes itself as an Austria-based broker regulated in Europe. Its Bitcoin page lists a long set of payment options. These include bank transfers and cards. PayPal and Klarna are listed too.

The page does not publish a fee figure or a minimum purchase, so read the quote before you confirm. It also does not list supported countries. Check eligibility before you create an account.

Fees and availability change often. Treat the table as a starting point and read each platform’s current terms.

Read the payment options column first. It shows whether you can start with a method you already trust. Then compare fees at your usual order size, because tiered fees change with the amount. A $50 purchase and a $5,000 purchase can carry very different percentages on the same platform. Last, check availability. A platform that does not serve your country is off the list.

Conclusion

The easiest option depends on how you want to pay and how often you plan to buy. Some platforms suit a single purchase. Others reward regular buying with lower fees.

Recurring buys deserve a look. They spread your purchases over time. That removes the pressure of picking one perfect entry price.

Start small for your first order. Read the final quote before you confirm. Check how long the payment takes to clear. Then decide whether to leave your Bitcoin on the platform or send it to your own wallet. If you choose a wallet, double-check the address before you send anything.

Keep a record of each purchase. Dates, amounts and fees help when you report taxes later. Tax rules differ by country, so check local guidance.

Finally, confirm that the platform operates in your country. Read its verification requirements before you deposit funds.

content:
U.S. pressure to hold Treasuries forces central banks to sell what they can, says Doomberg, setting up a wildly bullish long-term case for gold and Bitcoin.

What happens to reserve assets when you’re not allowed to sell them? Doomberg argues that U.S. pressure on allies to hold their Treasuries changes the math for central banks, and that in a crisis “you sell what you can sell, not what you want to sell.” That explains gold’s short-term weakness since February 28th, but in the long run he sees it as wildly bullish for gold and Bitcoin as neutral reserve assets. He also shares why younger, hyper-online generations are more likely to choose Bitcoin.

Friday, 30/10/2026 | 12:00 GMT by Sylwester Majewski

  • Recent consolidation in gold and major CFDs has compressed broker revenues, but early 2026 spikes in VIX above 30 suggest sharp volatility swings may soon return.
  • With the 3 November US midterms approaching, retail desks could see an influx of returning traders as election-driven uncertainty historically lifts transaction frequency.

Financial markets have experienced a period of relatively smaller activity in recent weeks, with several major instruments trading within narrow ranges. Gold, which has emerged as one of the main drivers of retail CFD trading volumes in recent years, has also experienced a period of consolidation.

For brokers, such conditions can translate into lower trading activity, fewer transactions and reduced revenue opportunities. The question is whether the current stagnation reflects a temporary pause before another period of increased market volatility. One potential catalyst is approaching. On 3 November 2026, the United States will hold its midterm elections, determining the composition of Congress for the remaining two years of President Donald Trump's term.

London's trading industry is coming home!

arket Volatility and Its Implications for Retail Trading Activity

Volatility is an important reason for trading activity in financial markets. Larger and more frequent price movements can create additional opportunities for speculative trading, encouraging existing investors to increase transaction frequency and attracting previously inactive traders back to the market. For retail brokers, whose revenues depend partly on trading activity, changes in market volatility can therefore have a real effect on business performance.

The relationship between expected and actual market volatility provides additional context. Finance Magnates Intelligence's comparison of VIX with one-month realised S&P 500 volatility shows that the two measures frequently move in the same direction, although the magnitude and timing of their movements differ. During February and March 2026, VIX rose above 30, while realised volatility increased subsequently, reaching approximately 20–22%. A similar relationship is visible in oil markets, where the Cboe Crude Oil ETF Volatility Index (OVX) climbed above 120 in February, preceding a substantial increase in realised oil volatility towards 80–90% during March.

These observations illustrate how elevated implied volatility can precede periods of stronger actual price fluctuations. They do not, by themselves, establish a corresponding increase in retail trading volumes, but they help explain why forward-looking volatility indicators may be relevant to brokers anticipating changes in market activity.

Correlation Between VIX and Retail CFD Trading Volumes

Is there any relationship between market volatility and retail CFD volumes? As our next chart shows, although retail volumes have followed a steady upward trend since January 2022, periods of increased VIX readings often coincide with higher retail CFD volumes. This suggests that market uncertainty attracts greater attention from retail investors, particularly when volatility rises sharply.

title: Formula 1’s 830 Million Fans Draw Forex and CFD Brokers to Global Sponsorships
summary:
Formula 1 has transformed into one of the world's fastest-growing sports
properties, reaching a global fanbase of more than 830 million people, a 12%
year-on-year increase. For brokers, the opportunity goes beyond brand
visibility, with partnerships increasingly becoming platforms for fan
engagement...
content:
Formula 1 has transformed into one of the world's fastest-growing sports properties, reaching a global fanbase of more than 830 million people, a 12% year-on-year increase. For brokers, the opportunity goes beyond brand visibility, with partnerships increasingly becoming platforms for fan engagement and brand activation.

The trend is particularly evident within the Forex and CFD sector, where an increasing number of brokers are leveraging F1 as a global marketing and brand-building platform. XMTrading, IC Markets, Libertex, Pepperstone, AvaTrade, INFINOX and Vantage are among the brands that have entered the F1 sponsorship landscape.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Meanwhile, FxPro stands out for the longevity of its involvement in the sport, with its current partnership with McLaren dating back to 2018, following earlier F1 team sponsorships with BMW Sauber and Virgin Racing.

According to Ampere Analysis, total Formula 1 sponsorship investment exceeded US$3 billion, with teams generating more than US$2 billion and Formula 1's commercial rights holders contributing the remaining US$1 billion.

SponsorUnited's Formula 1 Sponsorship Intelligence Report 2025 also highlights technology as the largest sponsoring sector, investing US$543 million, while financial services ranks as the second-largest category.

Team partnerships can command US$5 million–US$20 million per season, with high-profile partnerships potentially requiring significantly greater investment, making activation critical to maximising the value of the partnership.

Why Are Forex and CFD Brands Investing?

The growing presence of Forex and CFD brands in Formula 1 is unlikely to be coincidental.

As competition intensifies across the industry, firms are increasingly looking beyond traditional digital advertising to build stronger brand equity and earn traders' trust. Formula 1 provides a unique platform to achieve this through its global reach, premium positioning and year-round content ecosystem.

Formula 1 also embodies many of the same attributes that trading platforms seek to communicate: speed, precision, technology, continuous innovation and high-performance decision-making. This natural alignment allows sponsorships to feel authentic, creating stronger brand associations than traditional advertising alone.

What Makes Formula 1 Different?

1. Every Grand Prix Is a Unique Destination

Unlike traditional league competitions, where each match follows a similar format, every Formula 1 Grand Prix has its own identity.

Historic circuit venues such as Silverstone and Monza showcase the sport's rich heritage, while destination races in Monaco, Singapore, Miami, Las Vegas and Abu Dhabi offer completely different atmospheres and experiences.

Rather than repeating the same event every week, Forex and CFD firms gain a portfolio of unique destinations that can be tailored to different markets, client segments and business objectives throughout the season.

2. Formula 1 Is More Than a Sporting Event

Formula 1 has evolved into a lifestyle and entertainment platform rather than just a racing series. Race weekends increasingly combine elite motorsport with fine dining, luxury hospitality, live concerts, fashion, celebrity appearances and premium networking opportunities.

This broader ecosystem allows sponsors to engage audiences beyond traditional motorsport fans while positioning their brands alongside innovation, luxury and world-class experiences.

3. World-Class Hospitality Creates Business Value

Hospitality remains one of Formula 1's most powerful commercial assets. Experiences such as Paddock Club access, garage tours, pit lane walks, driver appearances and behind-the-scenes team access create unforgettable moments that few sports can match.

For Forex and CFD firms, these experiences provide valuable opportunities to strengthen relationships with introducing brokers, affiliates, institutional partners, VIP clients and prospective customers in a premium business environment where conversations often extend beyond the race itself.

4. One Partnership, a Truly Global Platform

For Forex and CFD brokers, growth rarely comes from a single region or market. Formula 1's truly global calendar gives brokers the opportunity to engage clients and business partners across North America, the GCC, Europe and Asia-Pacific, while its diverse hospitality offering allows brands to tailor experiences to different audiences, even within the same Grand Prix.

This enables brokers to build a consistent global brand while supporting regional customer acquisition, partner engagement and business development.

5. F1 Offers More Than Race-Day Exposure

Rather than relying on one-off promotions, brokers can keep partnerships relevant throughout the customer journey, making Formula 1 an always-on platform for brand building and customer engagement.

For instance, FxPro has used its McLaren partnership to create content-led activations, including its Strategy Debrief series, which provides behind-the-scenes insight into McLaren's race strategy and key decisions.

By bringing the team's expertise and decision-making process to audiences, the activation creates a natural connection between the high-stakes tactical decisions of F1 and the principles of precision and risk management in financial markets.

Pepperstone has taken a more experiential approach through its Aston Martin Aramco partnership, creating a range of client and partner experiences, including pit-lane dinners, Monaco yacht hospitality, driver meet-and-greets, garage tours and Silverstone track days.

These experiences give the broker a platform to deepen relationships with existing clients, create memorable touchpoints for prospects and engage business partners in a more personal setting.

Together, these examples illustrate how brokers can use F1 partnerships for more than brand visibility, creating ongoing opportunities to engage clients, prospects and partners throughout the season.

6. The Challenge of F1 Partnerships and Making Them Work

For brokers considering an investment in Formula 1, the first step is recognising that F1 is a truly global property. Unlike other sports sponsorships centred around relatively fixed home venues and regular matchday routines, every Grand Prix is a different operating environment.

The circuit, organisers, hospitality infrastructure, transport, local culture and surrounding events can all vary significantly. Delivering a premium guest experience therefore starts long before guests arrive at the track, from the first invitation and travel arrangements through to the final moment of the race weekend. The details matter.

There is also far more happening around a Grand Prix than the race itself. Concerts, fireside conversations, fan activities, paddock experiences and other events can create additional touchpoints throughout the weekend. For brokers hosting clients, prospects or business partners, these can become valuable components of a wider experience rather than simply being treated as ancillary benefits of the partnership.

The opportunity extends beyond the race weekend, too. Team factories, technical facilities and off-track access can create highly exclusive, money-can't-buy experiences. Fireside conversations with team principals, discussions with technical representatives, driver appearances and factory tours can give clients a different perspective on the sport while creating more meaningful engagement with the brand.

Perhaps most importantly, brokers should consider how the partnership can create value for both sides. The strongest partnerships are no longer simply about paying for rights and access; they can also involve integrating a broker's products, technology or services into the wider F1 ecosystem.

This creates the potential for two-way business case studies that demonstrate how the partnership delivers tangible value to the rights holder while giving the broker an authentic story to take to clients, prospects and relevant industry stakeholders.

Ultimately, making an F1 partnership work requires more than securing the rights. It requires understanding the complexity of the calendar, curating the experience around each race and finding ways for the brand and rights holder to create value together.

Final Thoughts

For Forex and CFD brands, the opportunity in Formula 1 goes well beyond securing visibility on a car or access to a race weekend. The global calendar, diverse hospitality, content opportunities and access to teams and talent create a platform that can be activated differently across markets and throughout the season.

But that opportunity also comes with complexity. Every Grand Prix presents a different environment, audience and set of possibilities, meaning the value of the partnership ultimately depends on how well a broker understands the ecosystem and connects it to its own commercial objectives.

The most effective F1 partnerships are therefore not simply sponsorships. They are platforms for creating experiences, building relationships and developing stories that have value for both the broker and the rights holder.

title: “An FTMO Ticker Sounds Really Cool”: FTMO’s Founders on Launching Futures and How the Prop Giant Made Bankers Like Them
summary: Fourteen years ago, in a trading club at the Prague University of Economics and Business, Otakar Šuffner and Marek Vašíček discovered a shared affinity for futures trading. When they founded FTMO in 2015, though, they had to be pragmatic. The retail prop trading industry was in its infancy, and the ...
content:
Fourteen years ago, in a trading club at the Prague University of Economics and Business, Otakar Šuffner and Marek Vašíček discovered a shared affinity for futures trading. When they founded FTMO in 2015, though, they had to be pragmatic. The retail prop trading industry was in its infancy, and the founders lacked both the capital and the business experience to navigate the complexities of futures. Instead, they built their business around CFDs, leveraging local industry connections, and became one of the better-known players in the industry. A month ago, they finally returned to their original passion. “So the time basically came this year. I like to say that Apple is also not releasing their products first. So it just took time,” Šuffner jokes.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Launching futures is merely the latest step in a wider campaign for the prop firm giant, which includes managing the operational realities behind the massive acquisition of legacy broker OANDA, navigating a fractured regulatory landscape and outmanoeuvring market volatility and predatory payout syndicates – all to build what they describe as a global “trading powerhouse.”

Futures Are Hot Now

Among the most intriguing shifts currently unfolding in the space is that futures-based prop offerings are becoming a new darling for funded traders. There’s good reason: industry pricing data indicate that a $100,000 futures evaluation costs roughly $190 on average, compared with about $420 for a $100,000 CFD/FX one.

Unsurprisingly, Šuffner notes that futures “were highly requested from our clients.”

FTMO Futures is officially LIVE. 🏆 The gold standard of prop trading, now powered for the exchange via Tradovate, NinjaTrader, and TradingView. No compromises. Just raw execution and total transparency. Explore FTMO Futures today 🙌🏻 https://t.co/g8HztyeUu4 https://t.co/WMDSy8DcRX

— FTMO.com (@FTMO_com) August 31, 2026

Futures had typically achieved these lower entry costs through a single-phase, subscription-style model. FTMO is following the same traditional model for its futures prop offering. Šuffner doesn’t want to speak to why others have abandoned the subscription model, but says, “We are always focusing on ourselves; we asked our clients what product they want to trade and we ended up with our current offering.”

Read more: Tradeify Co-Founders: “Difficult to Enter” Futures Prop; Subscription Ditch “Barely Moved Revenue”

The firm is determined to treat futures as a core business rather than an offering on the side, which means confronting established US incumbents like Topstep. Launching the product required a dedicated team and significant capital investment, essentially creating a new business next to their CFDs. However, Vašíček subtly downplays the friction. “I don’t think that the entry barriers are that high as in the regulated business, right?” he observes.

Still, while the global hub for futures trading is the US, the founders have been surprised by the international demand. “I was expecting that it would be US-heavy, but we have pretty much global customers, so at least for me it was very interesting,” Vašíček notes.

“We Made Those Bankers Like FTMO”

Like many in both the prop and broker space, FTMO is attempting to build a throughline, where a user can progress seamlessly from funded evaluations to a retail brokerage account, and eventually to a professional one.

The founders reveal that they initially explored acquiring smaller, regionally regulated brokers in Europe and Australia, and then planned to build this brokerage arm organically, hiring industry veterans in late 2024, including ex-Skilling CEO Michael Kamerman.

When the opportunity to acquire OANDA, which was globally established with licenses across most major hubs, from private equity firm CVC emerged, Vašíček admits his first reaction was to ask his co-founder, “‘Are you crazy?’ Then we realised that if we are serious about what we are doing, this is the one and only opportunity to have a global approach,” he explains.

Negotiating with elite private-equity dealmakers was an intense education for the founders, testing their operational maturity. “It was kind of eye-opening,” Šuffner says. "We were scheduling the calls at 3:00 am.”

FTMO secured a massive US$250 million syndicated credit line led by UniCredit, a significant milestone for a firm whose only previous corporate debt was a minor loan for mobile phones. “We made those bankers like FTMO and received the financing in record time for the Czech Republic,” Šuffner says.

Convincing conservative Czech bankers to finance the buyout – together with cash reserves, OANDA was acquired for about US$422 million – was only half the battle. Securing global regulatory approval took nearly ten months. Financial watchdogs scrutinised the founders heavily.

“They were very thorough; they were asking about our eye colour, our weight,” Šuffner recalls.

Vašíček chimes in, “Our compliance team knows absolutely everything about the two of us.”

Ultimately, they consider the deal as proof that a modern prop firm could meet the exacting standards of traditional finance. Vašíček says, “This is a great message for the industry, that a modern prop trading firm was able to prove to all parties that something serious like this could happen.”

“Credibility Is Not Done in Two Days; It’s Something You Need to Live By”

The model of FTMO to become what it calls a “trading powerhouse” has seen varying degrees of success elsewhere.

For one, platform providers have made launching prop firms effortless, leading to a flood of copycat firms vying for the same pie. The model also faces a threat from organised hedging groups that game these evaluation systems.

Related: Inside the 800-Member Trading Cartel Bleeding Prop Firms Dry

Platform providers have even tweaked their backends to account for hedging. For example, FPFX Tech, which provides the infrastructure for over 150 prop firms, has added risk-monitoring tools designed to flag abusive trading behaviour, including hedging.

“It’s something we need to take care of, but we built a lot of human capital and know-how on how it needs to be handled,” Vašíček says.

He also sees these ‘payout syndicates’ as unfair to users who follow the rules. He notes that back in university, they failed to secure jobs at traditional proprietary firms because, in his view, their CVs didn't meet the Ivy League criteria. “Prop firms are an opportunity, pretty much a life-changing opportunity, because I can become a trader. Now nobody cares about the pedigree,” he notes.

The founders believe that integrating FTMO’s model with OANDA’s 30-year positioning and reputation gives them a unique structural advantage in succeeding where others are failing. “Credibility is not done in two days; it’s something you need to live by,” Vašíček observes.

Regulation? What About It?

In 2024, the industry experienced a supply-chain shock when MetaQuotes abruptly revoked platform licenses from firms sub-leasing its software to serve US prop clients. The disruption prompted several prop firms to acquire small regulated brokerages simply to secure direct software licenses. Šuffner, though, maintains that FTMO’s acquisition of OANDA was never about that. “It was really about making the group stronger and delivering broader services,” he explains.

While prop trading appears to have fallen from ESMA’s priority list – the Paris-based agency having begun preliminary reviews in 2024 – the Dutch financial regulator recently ruled in January that instant funding accounts offered by a firm named Unfunded constituted CFD trading. As such, the firm was operating without a proper MiFID II license. The decision was upheld in court; it marks the first instance a European regulator has equated prop trading with investment services.

Šuffner notes that they have been closely monitoring this case, remaining attentive to potential regulatory developments and their broader implications for the industry.

Still, neither appears particularly worried about regulation, an attitude that is seemingly informed by their many interactions with watchdogs. Aside from the OANDA dealings, Šuffner notes that they “received a letter from the Spanish regulator” to explain their offering. Other regulators also have made inquiries, including ASIC.

The firm also has a substantial financial buffer to navigate any cost increases inside an emerging regulatory environment. In 2025, it reported revenues of approximately $420 million, representing a 31% year-on-year growth. “A regulated environment is a higher barrier, right? That means that there will be no hundreds of prop firms, but maybe tens of prop firms will remain,” Vašíček says.

Nonetheless, Šuffner wonders about the need to regulate simulated trading. “Regulation is here to protect the client, for good reason,” he says. “With prop firm clients, they are buying a service for a much smaller amount that they basically deposit money with a brokerage firm. So, is there even something to regulate?”

Among the most intriguing shifts currently unfolding in the space is that futures-based prop offerings are becoming a new darling for funded traders. There’s good reason: industry pricing data indicate that a $100,000 futures evaluation costs roughly $190 on average, compared with about $420 for a $100,000 CFD/FX one.

Unsurprisingly, Šuffner notes that futures “were highly requested from our clients.”

An IPO in the Horizon?

Despite record top-line growth, 2025 tested the firm's profitability. FTMO’s net income fell by 59% to roughly $37.5 million, a drop attributed to extreme market volatility. What with President Trump's dizzying tariff announcements, tech-sector anxieties and general geopolitical friction, it made predicting where the chips would fall difficult. FTMO missed its projected trader payout targets by 82%.

Interestingly, Šuffner treats this primarily as an accounting variance. “I honestly didn’t know about it. I just saw it in the articles,” he says. “It’s an accounting number, but from a company point of view is not something that would harm us in any way.”

As they navigate these market conditions, the founders are determined to conduct business on their own terms. They want to distance FTMO from the aggressive, lifestyle-focused marketing that proliferates in the industry.

“We never had aggressive marketing, never promised cars, dreams and miracles that are done in four days,” Vašíček emphasises. “For us, it is important to still stay FTMO. We are here for the long term. So we feel this sense of accountability and we want to do serious business and provide great service for the customers.”

For now, OANDA and FTMO are kept as two businesses with distinct management teams, though both founders serve as co-CEOs overseeing the overarching structure, a role Vašíček admits is demanding, yet exciting. Vašíček notes that while they are keeping an eye on new developments like prediction markets, they remain focused on their own roadmap rather than moving at the pace dictated by others. “Like every other business, we need to look around and always think about what's the future so we don't end up being dinosaurs,” he says.

Without shareholders pressing them, they have the freedom to remain patient and move to the beat of their own drum. As Šuffner highlights, “We own 100% of FTMO and OANDA.”

“An FTMO ticker sounds really cool,” Šuffner says, only half-joking.

title: Binance Confirms $6.3B Security Breach, Freezes $3B in Assets and Pledges Full Compensation
summary: Binance is investigating a security breach with an estimated $6.3 billion impact after attackers used compromised internal access to trigger unauthorized withdrawals across multiple blockchains.
content:
Skip to content

Binance is investigating a security breach with an estimated $6.3 billion impact after attackers used compromised internal access to trigger unauthorized withdrawals across multiple blockchains.

The exchange says blockchain partners have frozen approximately $3 billion in affected assets. Binance has also pledged to cover all losses through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company resources. However, the incident raises serious questions about its internal security controls and the safeguards protecting customer assets.

Binance Traces $6.3B Security Breach to Compromised DevOps Laptop

In an official security update published on October 30, Binance said its preliminary investigation pointed to a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. The attacker allegedly used the device to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.

Binance reports a $6.3 billion security breach involving a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop while confirming that no wallet private keys were exposed. Source: Binance/X

Binance stated that it had found no evidence of wallet private key exposure. However, that does not make the incident any less serious. The apparent ability to exploit an internal service and trigger legitimate withdrawal processes exposes a critical weakness in the exchange’s operational security. Private keys may have remained protected, but the systems authorized to move funds were apparently not sufficiently insulated from compromised internal access.

CZ assures users that funds remain SAFU and will be fully covered by the SAFU fund and company resources, while praising hundreds of employees for their overnight response efforts. Source: CZ/X

Independent blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs traced approximately $6.36 billion in transfers from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains on October 29. The transfers reportedly occurred within a relatively short period, with most of the movement taking place in approximately 20 minutes. The affected networks included Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, XRP Ledger, Solana, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, Base, and Polygon.

TRM Labs also attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean-linked hacking group, based on its on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The firm expressed high confidence in its assessment, although Binance has not publicly confirmed the attribution. TRM described the incident as the largest cryptocurrency theft on record, placing its estimated scale at more than four times the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025.

Nearly $3B Frozen as Tether and Circle Join Recovery Effort

Binance says approximately $3 billion in affected cryptocurrency has been frozen through cooperation with blockchain partners. The recovery effort involves law enforcement agencies, blockchain intelligence firms, and stablecoin issuers, including Tether and Circle.

Binance confirms it has frozen approximately $3 billion in assets linked to a major security breach affecting hot wallets across multiple blockchains. Source: Binance/X

The involvement of external companies has been particularly important because centralized stablecoin issuers can restrict transfers from identified addresses. Tether reportedly froze nearly $1.57 billion in assets connected to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. Binance co-CEO Yi He also said Ripple had frozen approximately $200 million associated with the attack.

TRM Labs’ on-chain assessment put the total amount frozen at approximately $2.7 billion, including assets restricted by stablecoin issuers and emergency action taken by the Arbitrum Security Council. The difference from Binance’s rounded $3 billion figure reflects the different reporting snapshots and tracking scope.

Despite these interventions, freezing assets does not automatically mean the funds have been returned to Binance or their rightful owners. TRM estimated that attackers still controlled approximately $2.4 billion in cryptocurrency at the time of its assessment, including substantial amounts of Bitcoin and Ether. The remaining funds could prove considerably harder to recover if they move through decentralized exchanges, lending protocols, bridges, or other services.

The incident also highlights an uncomfortable reality for Binance. A substantial part of the recovery effort has depended on other companies identifying suspicious wallets and restricting the movement of assets after the withdrawals occurred. For an exchange handling billions of dollars in customer transactions, the effectiveness of preventive security controls deserves at least as much scrutiny as the industry’s response after the breach.

Binance Withdrawals Remain Suspended as Users Face Trading Disruptions

Binance initially suspended both deposits and withdrawals while its security team investigated the incident, revoked authorization for the affected address, and reviewed its withdrawal infrastructure.

Binance confirms deposits remain operational, while withdrawals are suspended for up to 48 hours to complete security upgrades. Source: Binance/X

The exchange later clarified that deposits were operating normally, while withdrawals remained paused during a security overhaul. Binance said it expected to begin restoring withdrawal services within 48 hours. However, that timeline represents an expected resumption rather than confirmation that all withdrawal functions have returned to normal.

The suspension also created practical problems for customers who needed access to their assets during volatile market conditions. One user posting as OkanErtem07 reported that a ZRO withdrawal had remained in “Processing” for hours, leaving the user unable to cancel the request or trade the tokens. The user claimed that the delay prevented a planned sale near $1.60 before the token price declined.

Okan Ertem reports that Binance’s security freeze left his ZRO withdrawal stuck in processing, preventing cancellation or trading and causing him to miss a $1.60 sale before prices declined. Source: @OkanErtem07/X

Although this individual account has not been independently verified, it illustrates an important consequence of exchange-wide security suspensions. Customers can face losses or missed trading opportunities even when their account balances remain intact. A withdrawal restriction can effectively prevent users from responding to market movements, managing positions, or moving assets to alternative platforms.

Binance’s assurance that customer funds are safe therefore does not address every concern created by the incident. Customers also need reliable access to their holdings and clear information about pending transactions, withdrawal backlogs, and service restoration.

Binance Pledges Full Compensation and Updated Proof of Reserves

Binance has committed to covering all losses associated with the security incident using its SAFU fund and company resources. The pledge is intended to reassure customers that the estimated $6.3 billion impact will not translate into losses for their account balances.

Binance pledges to fully cover all losses resulting from the major security incident. Source: Binance/X

However, the exchange has yet to publish a complete technical explanation of the breach or provide a detailed breakdown of how its compensation process will operate. Its announcement does not explain how the final losses will be calculated, how recovery efforts will affect the amount ultimately covered, or whether any additional customer claims will require separate procedures.

The SAFU fund, established to provide an emergency financial buffer for users, is central to Binance’s commitment. Nevertheless, customers should not have to rely solely on public assurances when an incident of this scale exposes weaknesses in the systems responsible for protecting their assets.

Binance has also promised to publish an updated Proof of Reserves after completing the security remediation. The update could help provide a clearer view of the exchange’s asset backing following the incident. However, reserve disclosures alone cannot establish whether internal access controls, transaction authorization processes, and withdrawal monitoring systems are secure.

The company has promised a detailed technical post-mortem once investigators verify the facts. That report will be particularly important in determining how a compromised employee device gained access to withdrawal infrastructure, why existing safeguards failed to prevent unauthorized transactions, and what changes will stop similar attacks.

For now, Binance faces two separate challenges: recovering the remaining cryptocurrency and restoring confidence in the security of its platform. Its compensation pledge addresses the immediate financial concern, but it does not erase the operational failure behind the breach. The real test will be whether Binance can provide verifiable answers, restore normal withdrawal services, and demonstrate that its security infrastructure has been fundamentally strengthened.

title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Carbon and Genie 4 AI Models With Native Audio and Photorealistic Simulations
summary: Google has introduced Gemini 4 Carbon and Genie 4, expanding its artificial intelligence portfolio with advances in cybersecurity, software development, and interactive world simulation.
content:
Skip to content

Google has introduced Gemini 4 Carbon and Genie 4, expanding its artificial intelligence portfolio with advances in cybersecurity, software development, and interactive world simulation.

Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon focuses on complex reasoning, secure code generation, and long-running agentic tasks, while Genie 4 creates interactive environments with photorealistic visuals and native audio.

The announcements highlight two distinct areas of AI development. Carbon targets demanding technical and security workloads, while Genie 4 aims to generate dynamic digital worlds that respond to user instructions in real time. Both models are being introduced through limited-access programs before broader availability.

Gemini 4 Carbon Tops Intelligence and Cybersecurity Benchmarks

Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced Gemini 4 Carbon as the newest frontier model in the Gemini 4 family. Its release follows Gemini 4 Argon, which arrived approximately two weeks earlier, underscoring the pace of development within Google’s AI lineup.

Gemini 4 Carbon delivers improved performance over its predecessor Argon, with advanced cybersecurity capabilities and enhanced support for long-running agentic tasks. Source: Google via X

According to the supplied benchmark results, Carbon ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, scoring 59 points. The model also records strong results across several cybersecurity evaluations, including 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for vulnerability detection, 54.8% on ExploitGym, and 71.0% on CWE-bench for software patching.

These benchmarks assess different capabilities, from identifying security weaknesses to evaluating how effectively a model can address vulnerabilities. Their results offer measurable indicators of performance, although scores across separate evaluations do not necessarily translate directly into better outcomes in every real-world environment.

Google also reports substantial improvements over Gemini 4 Argon in long-horizon tasks, agentic coding, and multimodal understanding. Secure code generation reportedly delivers a twofold improvement, while the model’s safeguards are designed to reduce susceptibility to indirect prompt injection attacks.

The supplied announcement describes Carbon as achieving perfect resistance to indirect prompt injection in the reported evaluation. This result should be understood within the scope of that test rather than as proof of immunity to every prompt injection technique or cybersecurity threat.

Gemini 4 Carbon Demonstrates Advanced 3D Modeling Capabilities

Gemini 4 Carbon has also attracted attention for its performance in computer-aided design (CAD) and complex 3D modeling. A side-by-side video shared by AI tracker @Mr_Salio compares the model with Opus 5.5 on a detailed airplane-design task.

The post compares Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon with Opus 5.5 in a side-by-side video demonstration of complex 3D airplane modeling. Source: @Mr_Salio via X

The demonstration focuses on technically demanding features, including X-ray views, exploded assemblies, and intricate internal components. The aircraft models reportedly contain between 1,400 and more than 2,600 parts, requiring the system to maintain structural consistency across numerous connected elements.

In the comparison, Carbon appears to handle internal assemblies and complex views with greater coherence and detail. Such capabilities could be useful for engineering visualization, product design, and other workflows in which models must preserve relationships between components.

However, a demonstration video alone does not establish how consistently a model performs across professional CAD workloads. Independent testing would be needed to assess dimensional accuracy, editability, engineering constraints, and reliability in production environments.

Google Begins Gemini 4 Carbon Rollout Through Fairwind

Google is initially making Gemini 4 Carbon available to selected cybersecurity professionals through its Fairwind Program. The staged rollout is intended to gather feedback on the model’s capabilities, safety measures, and suitability for security-related tasks before wider access.

Google is gradually releasing Gemini 4 Carbon to trusted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program, with enhanced safeguards against prompt injection and model misalignment ahead of wider access. Source: Sundar Pichai via X

The approach reflects the challenges of releasing powerful AI systems that can assist with vulnerability discovery and software security. These capabilities may help defenders identify weaknesses and develop fixes, but they also require safeguards against misuse.

Google plans to expand access to developers and other users in the near future. The supplied announcement lists introductory API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. These figures represent the stated initial rates, which may be subject to the terms of the eventual public release.

The company also highlights improvements in resistance to prompt injection and reductions in misalignment rates. The effectiveness of these protections will depend on how the model behaves across different applications, attack methods, and deployment conditions.

Genie 4 Generates Photorealistic Worlds With Native Audio

Alongside Carbon, Google DeepMind has introduced Genie 4, an interactive world model designed to generate dynamic environments with realistic visuals, physical movement, and synchronized audio.

Google DeepMind unveiled Genie 4, an interactive world model that generates photorealistic simulations with native audio and maintains consistency through Gemini integration. Source: Google via X

Unlike a conventional video generator that produces a fixed sequence of frames, an interactive world model allows users to influence what happens inside a generated environment. Genie 4 supports real-time text instructions that can change scenes, camera angles, and actions as a simulation unfolds.

Native audio is another central feature. Generated environments can include ambient sounds, music, engine noise, and character dialogue, adding an audio layer that responds to events within the simulated world.

Google’s demonstrations illustrate how these capabilities work together. In one 50-second example, a first-person motorcycle journey begins at a red traffic light on a sunlit coastal highway. A text instruction changes the light to green, after which the motorcycle accelerates along the road. Engine revs, ocean waves, and passing traffic accompany the movement.

Other demonstrations reportedly include dragon flights, crowded train stations, and robotic systems handling liquids. These examples showcase the model’s ability to combine visual detail, physical interactions, and changing scene conditions.

Gemini integration also helps Genie 4 track the state of its simulated environment and coordinate multi-step events. This is important for maintaining continuity as objects move, actions unfold, and users modify the scene.

Genie 4 Access Expands Through Project Genie and Gemini API

Genie 4 is currently available as a research preview for trusted testers. Google plans to extend access to Google AI Ultra subscribers through Project Genie, while selected partners are expected to receive early access through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

Sundar Pichai unveiled Genie 4, Google’s advanced world model featuring real-time environment control, dynamic actions, and native audio with realistic dialogue. Source: Sundar Pichai via X

The limited rollout gives Google an opportunity to evaluate the system before making it more widely available. As with other generative AI tools, practical performance will depend on the complexity of the requested environment, the consistency of interactions, and the model’s ability to preserve realistic behavior over time.

Interactive world models could support several applications beyond entertainment. In robotics, generated environments may help researchers test control systems and explore scenarios that would be expensive, difficult, or unsafe to reproduce physically. Developers could also use the technology for simulation, virtual prototyping, and interactive experiences.

Nevertheless, simulated environments do not automatically reproduce every constraint of the physical world. Robotics and engineering applications will require careful validation to determine whether generated scenarios provide sufficiently accurate conditions for training and testing.

Google Advances AI Across Coding and Interactive Simulation

Gemini 4 Carbon and Genie 4 address different but complementary areas of AI development. Carbon emphasizes reasoning, cybersecurity, and complex technical workflows, while Genie 4 focuses on generating interactive worlds with realistic visuals, physics, and sound.

Their initial releases remain limited, and broader availability will provide more opportunities to evaluate performance outside curated demonstrations and benchmark environments. For Carbon, key questions include how reliably it detects vulnerabilities and produces secure code. For Genie 4, the focus will be on consistency, real-time responsiveness, and the accuracy of simulated interactions.

Google’s announcements illustrate a wider effort to develop AI systems that can do more than generate text or images. By combining advanced reasoning with specialized capabilities, the company is targeting applications ranging from software security and engineering to simulation and robotics. The models’ practical value will ultimately depend on their reliability, safety, and performance in real-world use.
